# dissolve: full documentation

> Animated components you own, for React Native and React. npx dissolve-ui add copies the source into your app; the React Native engine turns any view into dust (Skia, Reanimated 4).

Every page of https://dissolve.rselmi.com as markdown: the docs, then every component, then every effect. The summary with links is https://dissolve.rselmi.com/llms.txt.

---

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/introduction/

# dissolve

An animation library for React Native, with its components for React on the web too. Wrap any view and it dissolves, melts, peels or rebuilds itself. Sixteen variants, all on the UI thread.

`dissolve-ui` gives deletes, archives, arrivals and gestures a physical ending. Wrap your app once, put a ref on a view, call `dissolve()`.

## How it works

1. **Snapshot.** Skia captures the view with `makeImageFromView`, so any view works: text, images, blur, gradients.
2. **Grains.** The image is cut into a grid of grains drawn with a single `<Atlas>`, capped at 6000 per effect.
3. **UI thread.** Every grain is moved in one Reanimated 4 reaction per frame, idle grains are skipped, haptics follow the motion.

## Two parts

1. **The engine, from npm.** `npm install dissolve-ui` gives you the provider and the hooks: `useDissolve`, `DissolveIn`, `useAppear`, the gesture and transition hooks. Every variant in the sidebar runs on it.
2. **Components, copied into your app.** Swipe to delete, toasts, slide to confirm and the rest are not in the package. `npx dissolve-ui add` copies their source into `components/dissolve`, the shadcn way: the code is yours, styled with classNames and the `--dissolve-*` theme tokens.
3. **React Native or React.** `npx dissolve-ui init` asks which one and saves it in `dissolve.json`. On the web, components take the same props, need only React 19 and `react-dom`, and draw on a canvas: no engine to install. Each component page has a switch for its React Native and React snippets.
- [See the Gallery](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/)
- [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)
- [CLI](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/cli/)
- [Use it with your agent](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/agent-prompt/)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/introduction/

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/agent-prompt/

# Agent prompt

The fastest way to set up dissolve. Paste this prompt into your coding agent: it installs the engine, sets up NativeWind and adds the components you want.

Tell your coding agent

```
Add dissolve-ui to this React Native / Expo app. It snapshots any view with Skia and turns it into grains animated on the UI thread (Reanimated 4).

1. Install the package and its peers:
   npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
   (Known good: Expo SDK 57, Skia 2.6, Reanimated 4.5, react-native-worklets 0.10, gesture handler 2.32. Bare React Native needs 'react-native-worklets/plugin' in babel.config.js.)

2. Wrap the root layout once, above the navigator, inside GestureHandlerRootView:
   <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
     <DissolveProvider><Stack /></DissolveProvider>
   </GestureHandlerRootView>
   Do not add a second provider if one exists.

3. Use the hook on the view that should disappear:
   const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();
   <View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>...</View>
   await dissolve({ preset: 'dust' });
   then remove the item from state. Never unmount the view before the await resolves.

4. Ready-made components (swipe to delete, toasts, like button, slide to confirm, OTP input, thinking orb, mini player...) are not exported by the package. They are copied into the project with the CLI, shadcn style, and need NativeWind v5 (Tailwind v4 on react-native-css) plus tailwind-merge. Skip a) if NativeWind v5 already runs in the app.
   a) NativeWind v5 on Expo SDK 57:
      npm pkg set overrides.lightningcss=1.30.1
      npm install --legacy-peer-deps nativewind@5.0.0-preview.4 react-native-css@3.0.7 tailwindcss@^4 @tailwindcss/postcss tailwind-merge
      metro.config.js: module.exports = withNativewind(getDefaultConfig(__dirname), { inlineVariables: false, globalClassNamePolyfill: false }) (withNativewind from 'nativewind/metro')
      postcss.config.mjs: export default { plugins: { '@tailwindcss/postcss': {} } };
      nativewind-env.d.ts: /// <reference types="react-native-css/types" />
      global.css starts with: @import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme); @import "tailwindcss/preflight.css" layer(base); @import "tailwindcss/utilities.css"; and is imported once at the top of the root layout.
   b) npx dissolve-ui init --native   (once: dissolve.json, tw.tsx primitives + --dissolve-* theme tokens in global.css, then it checks the setup and prints what is missing: fix everything it reports)
   c) npx dissolve-ui add <name>      (npx dissolve-ui list shows the names; dependencies between components are copied too)
      import { SlideToConfirm } from '@/components/dissolve/slide-to-confirm';
   Restyle with className and the part classNames (textClassName, boxClassName...), or change the --dissolve-* tokens in global.css. Light and dark follow the system.
   Finish by running npx tsc --noEmit and starting the app.

Pick the variant from the intent:
- Exits (useDissolve): delete a row or card: dust. Delete forever: sand. Unsend or burn: ember. Tap to pop: snap with origin { x: locationX, y: locationY }. Error or broken: shatter. Playful: melt. Clear all: field: 'cascade' with rows (local Y of each row) on the list container.
- Archive or move: stream with to: iconRef and onArrive to bump the icon.
- Entrances: new message or card: <DissolveIn preset="gather">. List: <DissolveIn preset="rain" delay={i * 40}>. Generated text: useAppear().appear({ preset: 'print' }).
- Gestures: swipe to dismiss: fling with the release velocity, or useDissolveScrub({ preset, onCommit }) for a reversible drag. Sticker or card dismissal by hand: useDissolvePeel({ onCommit }), both return { ref, gesture, style } for a GestureDetector around an Animated.View. Destructive confirm (delete account, wipe data): useDissolveHold({ onCommit }) instead of an alert, spread pressHandlers on a Pressable.
- Transitions: toggle state (Follow to Following): useDissolveMorph. Leave a screen: useDissolveScreen().dissolveScreen({ preset: 'sand', then: () => router.back() }).

Rules:
- One effect per user action, on user intent only, 0.9 s to 1.8 s.
- Reduced motion is handled by the provider (the effect is skipped), do not add a custom fallback.
- Keep grain counts reasonable: default grain on cards, a larger grain on big views, useDissolveScreen for full screens, one cascade burst instead of one burst per row.
- Import the engine and hooks from dissolve-ui. Import components from their copied file, never from the package.

For a React web app (Next.js, Vite) there is no engine to install: run npx dissolve-ui init --web, then npx dissolve-ui add <name> (npx dissolve-ui list shows which components run on the web). The components need React 19 and react-dom only, and take the same props as on native.
```

## Keep it in your agent

Install the skill or the MCP server once, and your agent knows dissolve in every project.

Claude Code

Install the skill

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/dissolve-ui && curl -fsSL https://dissolve.rselmi.com/skills/dissolve/SKILL.md -o ~/.claude/skills/dissolve-ui/SKILL.md
```

Add the MCP server

```sh
claude mcp add dissolve -- npx -y dissolve-ui-mcp
```

Codex

Add the instructions to AGENTS.md

```sh
curl -fsSL https://dissolve.rselmi.com/skills/dissolve/SKILL.md >> AGENTS.md
```

Add the MCP server

```sh
codex mcp add dissolve -- npx -y dissolve-ui-mcp
```

## Details

## Claude skill

An Agent Skill is a `SKILL.md` file Claude loads on its own whenever you ask for a dissolve effect. It holds the setup, the API of every hook, a variant picking table and the best practices.

SKILL.md

dissolve-ui

- [View](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/skills/dissolve/SKILL.md)
- [Download](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/skills/dissolve/SKILL.md)

For all your projects

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/dissolve-ui && curl -fsSL https://dissolve.rselmi.com/skills/dissolve/SKILL.md -o ~/.claude/skills/dissolve-ui/SKILL.md
```

For this project only, shared with your team

```sh
mkdir -p .claude/skills/dissolve-ui && curl -fsSL https://dissolve.rselmi.com/skills/dissolve/SKILL.md -o .claude/skills/dissolve-ui/SKILL.md
```

Restart Claude Code, then ask for an effect, for example "dissolve the row when I delete a task". With other agents, paste the file into `AGENTS.md` or a Cursor rule.

## MCP server

A tiny MCP server with no dependencies, published on npm as `dissolve-ui-mcp`. Your agent runs it with `npx` over stdio, so it stays up to date, and it answers with the same data as the docs. The source is in `mcp/server.mjs` on [GitHub](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve).

| Tool | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `list_variants` | Every variant with its kind (exit, entrance, gesture, transition), hook and use case. |
| `get_variant` | Usage snippet, options and best practices for one variant. |
| `get_setup` | Install command, provider snippet, first effect, the component CLI and picking rules. |

Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add dissolve -- npx -y dissolve-ui-mcp
```

Claude Desktop · claude_desktop_config.json:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dissolve": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "dissolve-ui-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Cursor · .cursor/mcp.json:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dissolve": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "dissolve-ui-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Codex · ~/.codex/config.toml:

```toml
[mcp_servers.dissolve]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "dissolve-ui-mcp"]
```

Then ask: "use the dissolve MCP to add a delete effect to the inbox rows".

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/agent-prompt/

# Installation

Paste one prompt into your coding agent and it sets up everything: engine, provider, NativeWind and components. Or follow the steps by hand.

## With your agent

Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any chat. It installs the engine, wraps the root layout, sets up NativeWind v5, runs `init` and adds the components you ask for. More options, like the skill and the MCP server, are on the [Agent prompt](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/agent-prompt/) page.

Tell your coding agent

```
Add dissolve-ui to this React Native / Expo app. It snapshots any view with Skia and turns it into grains animated on the UI thread (Reanimated 4).

1. Install the package and its peers:
   npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
   (Known good: Expo SDK 57, Skia 2.6, Reanimated 4.5, react-native-worklets 0.10, gesture handler 2.32. Bare React Native needs 'react-native-worklets/plugin' in babel.config.js.)

2. Wrap the root layout once, above the navigator, inside GestureHandlerRootView:
   <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
     <DissolveProvider><Stack /></DissolveProvider>
   </GestureHandlerRootView>
   Do not add a second provider if one exists.

3. Use the hook on the view that should disappear:
   const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();
   <View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>...</View>
   await dissolve({ preset: 'dust' });
   then remove the item from state. Never unmount the view before the await resolves.

4. Ready-made components (swipe to delete, toasts, like button, slide to confirm, OTP input, thinking orb, mini player...) are not exported by the package. They are copied into the project with the CLI, shadcn style, and need NativeWind v5 (Tailwind v4 on react-native-css) plus tailwind-merge. Skip a) if NativeWind v5 already runs in the app.
   a) NativeWind v5 on Expo SDK 57:
      npm pkg set overrides.lightningcss=1.30.1
      npm install --legacy-peer-deps nativewind@5.0.0-preview.4 react-native-css@3.0.7 tailwindcss@^4 @tailwindcss/postcss tailwind-merge
      metro.config.js: module.exports = withNativewind(getDefaultConfig(__dirname), { inlineVariables: false, globalClassNamePolyfill: false }) (withNativewind from 'nativewind/metro')
      postcss.config.mjs: export default { plugins: { '@tailwindcss/postcss': {} } };
      nativewind-env.d.ts: /// <reference types="react-native-css/types" />
      global.css starts with: @import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme); @import "tailwindcss/preflight.css" layer(base); @import "tailwindcss/utilities.css"; and is imported once at the top of the root layout.
   b) npx dissolve-ui init --native   (once: dissolve.json, tw.tsx primitives + --dissolve-* theme tokens in global.css, then it checks the setup and prints what is missing: fix everything it reports)
   c) npx dissolve-ui add <name>      (npx dissolve-ui list shows the names; dependencies between components are copied too)
      import { SlideToConfirm } from '@/components/dissolve/slide-to-confirm';
   Restyle with className and the part classNames (textClassName, boxClassName...), or change the --dissolve-* tokens in global.css. Light and dark follow the system.
   Finish by running npx tsc --noEmit and starting the app.

Pick the variant from the intent:
- Exits (useDissolve): delete a row or card: dust. Delete forever: sand. Unsend or burn: ember. Tap to pop: snap with origin { x: locationX, y: locationY }. Error or broken: shatter. Playful: melt. Clear all: field: 'cascade' with rows (local Y of each row) on the list container.
- Archive or move: stream with to: iconRef and onArrive to bump the icon.
- Entrances: new message or card: <DissolveIn preset="gather">. List: <DissolveIn preset="rain" delay={i * 40}>. Generated text: useAppear().appear({ preset: 'print' }).
- Gestures: swipe to dismiss: fling with the release velocity, or useDissolveScrub({ preset, onCommit }) for a reversible drag. Sticker or card dismissal by hand: useDissolvePeel({ onCommit }), both return { ref, gesture, style } for a GestureDetector around an Animated.View. Destructive confirm (delete account, wipe data): useDissolveHold({ onCommit }) instead of an alert, spread pressHandlers on a Pressable.
- Transitions: toggle state (Follow to Following): useDissolveMorph. Leave a screen: useDissolveScreen().dissolveScreen({ preset: 'sand', then: () => router.back() }).

Rules:
- One effect per user action, on user intent only, 0.9 s to 1.8 s.
- Reduced motion is handled by the provider (the effect is skipped), do not add a custom fallback.
- Keep grain counts reasonable: default grain on cards, a larger grain on big views, useDissolveScreen for full screens, one cascade burst instead of one burst per row.
- Import the engine and hooks from dissolve-ui. Import components from their copied file, never from the package.

For a React web app (Next.js, Vite) there is no engine to install: run npx dissolve-ui init --web, then npx dissolve-ui add <name> (npx dissolve-ui list shows which components run on the web). The components need React 19 and react-dom only, and take the same props as on native.
```

## React on the web

Building a Next.js or Vite app? Skip the engine and NativeWind: web components need React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else. `init` asks the platform (React is preselected in a web project), saves it in `dissolve.json` and writes the theme tokens, as plain CSS when the project has no Tailwind.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui init --web
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add scratch-card
```

app/page.tsx:

```tsx
import { ScratchCard } from '@/components/dissolve/scratch-card';

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <ScratchCard onReveal={claim}>
      <span className="text-4xl font-bold">$25</span>
    </ScratchCard>
  );
}
```

Same props as on React Native. `npx dissolve-ui list` shows which components run on the web, and every component page has a React Native / React switch.

Using shadcn? `npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/scratch-card.json` works too, see [CLI](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/cli/).

## React Native, by hand

## Install the engine

The package holds the engine and the hooks. It is all you need for the variants.

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

| Peer | Tested | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@shopify/react-native-skia` | 2.6 | Snapshot and Atlas drawing |
| `react-native-reanimated` | 4.5 | UI thread animation |
| `react-native-worklets` | 0.10 | Worklets runtime for Reanimated 4 |
| `react-native-gesture-handler` | 2.32 | Scrub, peel and hold gestures |
| `expo-haptics` | 57 | Haptic ticks during the effect |

Built on Expo SDK 57 and React Native 0.86, runs in Expo Go. Expo's Babel preset already adds the worklets plugin. In a bare React Native app, add `'react-native-worklets/plugin'` to `babel.config.js`.

## Add the provider

The provider draws grains in a full screen overlay that ignores touches. Put it above your navigator so an effect survives a screen pop.

app/_layout.tsx:

```tsx
import { Stack } from 'expo-router';
import { GestureHandlerRootView } from 'react-native-gesture-handler';
import { DissolveProvider } from 'dissolve-ui';

export default function Layout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <DissolveProvider>
        <Stack />
      </DissolveProvider>
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

## Quick start

Put the ref on the view to snapshot, hide it while it dissolves, and remove the item once the promise resolves.

Row.tsx:

```tsx
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native';
import { useDissolve } from 'dissolve-ui';

export function Row({ item, onRemove }) {
  const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();

  return (
    <Pressable onPress={async () => {
      await dissolve({ preset: 'sand' });
      onRemove(item.id); // the space can be reclaimed
    }}>
      <View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>
        {/* row content */}
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

Reduced motion is handled for you: the effect is skipped and the view hides at once.

## Components

Components are copied into your project instead of imported from the package, like shadcn. You own the file, edit it freely, and restyle it with classNames. They need NativeWind v5 (Tailwind v4 on `react-native-css`) and `tailwind-merge`.

## Set up NativeWind v5

Skip this step if your app already runs NativeWind v5.

```sh
npx expo install nativewind@5.0.0-preview.4 react-native-css@3.0.7 tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss tailwind-merge
```

| Package | Tested | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nativewind` | 5.0.0-preview.4 | className on React Native views |
| `react-native-css` | 3.0.7 | The CSS runtime behind NativeWind v5 |
| `tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/postcss` | 4 | Tailwind v4 compiler |
| `tailwind-merge` | 3 | Your classes win over the defaults |
| `lightningcss (override)` | 1.30.1 | Pinned for Expo SDK 57 |

On Expo SDK 57, pin `lightningcss` with npm `overrides` (`resolutions` is Yarn only), then reinstall with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`.

package.json:

```json
{
  "overrides": {
    "lightningcss": "1.30.1"
  }
}
```

metro.config.js:

```js
const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config');
const { withNativewind } = require('nativewind/metro');

const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);

module.exports = withNativewind(config, {
  inlineVariables: false,         // keeps the theme tokens live, light and dark
  globalClassNamePolyfill: false, // className comes from the tw primitives
});
```

postcss.config.mjs:

```js
export default {
  plugins: {
    '@tailwindcss/postcss': {},
  },
};
```

global.css:

```css
@import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme);
@import "tailwindcss/preflight.css" layer(base);
@import "tailwindcss/utilities.css";

/* npx dissolve-ui init appends the dissolve tokens below */
```

Import `global.css` once at the top of `app/_layout.tsx`. The full guide is on [nativewind.dev](https://www.nativewind.dev/v5).

## Init

Once per project. It asks the platform (React Native is preselected in an Expo or React Native project) and saves it in `dissolve.json`, writes `tw.tsx`, the className primitives every component shares, and appends the theme tokens to your `global.css`. It also tells you which dependency is missing.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui init
```

## Add components

Name one or more. Files land in `components/dissolve`, or `src/components/dissolve` with a `src/` layout, and the CLI prints the import line.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add slide-to-confirm swipe-to-delete
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui list
```

Checkout.tsx:

```tsx
import { SlideToConfirm } from '@/components/dissolve/slide-to-confirm';

<SlideToConfirm
  label="Slide to pay 42 €"
  doneLabel="Paid"
  onConfirm={pay}
  className="mx-4"
/>
```

Every option is on the [CLI](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/cli/) page. Every component page shows its own `add` command and props.

## Theme

Components read `--dissolve-*` tokens: `background`, `surface`, `surface-2`, `foreground`, `muted`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `success`, `danger`, `danger-foreground`, `accent`, `border`, `chart-1` to `chart-3`. Change a value in `global.css` and every component follows. Dark values sit in a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block, so dark mode follows the system.

For one instance, pass a className. Classes are merged with `tailwind-merge`, so yours replace the default of the same kind: `className="bg-amber-100"` replaces `bg-dissolve-surface`.

Order.tsx:

```tsx
// Defaults: track bg-dissolve-surface, number text-dissolve-foreground
<SlideToConfirm
  label="Slide to order"
  onConfirm={order}
  className="bg-amber-100"                      // replaces bg-dissolve-surface
/>

<NumberTicker
  value={total}
  textClassName="text-emerald-600 font-bold"    // replaces the color and the weight
/>
```

- [Pick a variant](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/)
- [Theming](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/theming/)
- [Let your agent do it](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/agent-prompt/)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/cli/

# CLI

Copy components into your project, the shadcn way. The source is yours to read, edit and restyle.

One CLI for React Native and React on the web, run it with `npx`. Native components need NativeWind v5 in the project, web components only React 19, see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/). `npx dissolve-ui` runs the same CLI.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui init
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add swipe-to-delete toast
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui list
```

## Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | Asks the platform, React Native or React, with the one your `package.json` points to preselected, and saves it in `dissolve.json`. Appends the theme tokens to your `global.css`, and on native writes `tw.tsx` (className primitives, `cn`, `useToken`). Then lists missing dependencies. |
| `add <name...>` | Copies one or more components for the platform in `dissolve.json`, running `init` first if it is missing, and prints the import line of each file. |
| `list` | Every component, the platforms it runs on and a one line description. Alias: `ls`. |
| `help` | Usage. Also `--help` or `-h`. |

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--native, --web` | asked | Pick the platform without the question. Saved in `dissolve.json`. |
| `--yes, -y` | off | Take the detected platform. Also what happens without a terminal, in CI or scripts. |
| `--path, -p <dir>` | `components/dissolve` | Target folder, relative to the project. |
| `--overwrite, -o` | off | Replace files that exist. Without it, existing files are skipped so your edits are safe. With `init`, appends the tokens again. |
| `--cwd <dir>` | current folder | Project root, for monorepos and scripts. |

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add otp-input --path app/ui/dissolve --overwrite
```

## Platform

`init` preselects React Native when `package.json` has `react-native` or `expo`, React when it has `react-dom`, `next` or `vite` without them. The answer goes in `dissolve.json` at the project root, and every `add` reads it. Run `init --web` or `init --native` to switch.

dissolve.json:

```json
{
  "platform": "web",
  "dir": "components/dissolve"
}
```

## Where files go

By default `components/dissolve`. When `tsconfig.json` maps `@/*` to `./src/*` and a `src` folder exists, `src/components/dissolve`. Import lines use your `@/` alias when there is one, a relative path otherwise.

Terminal:

```sh
$ npx dissolve-ui add toast like-button
added   components/dissolve/toast.tsx
        import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@/components/dissolve/toast';
added   components/dissolve/like-button.tsx
        import { LikeButton } from '@/components/dissolve/like-button';
```

## With the shadcn CLI

Already on shadcn? Every component is also a shadcn registry item. Pass its URL to `shadcn add`, no `init` or `dissolve.json` needed. The React item lives at `/r/<name>.json`, the React Native one at `/r/native/<name>.json`.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/scratch-card.json
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/scratch-card.json
```

shadcn follows the dependencies for you: the component, its core, the shared files (engine, kit, the React hook, or `tw.tsx` on native) and the npm packages. Shared files are installed once, however many components you add. Files land in `components/dissolve`, the same place as with the dissolve CLI.

The theme tokens come as a `dissolve-theme` item: shadcn writes them in your CSS, light on `:root` and dark on `.dark`, the class shadcn projects already toggle. On React Native, you still install the engine and wrap the app in `<DissolveProvider>`, see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/).

The full list is in [registry.json](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/registry.json) and [native/registry.json](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/registry.json).

## What init writes

On the web, `dissolve.json` and the theme tokens, as plain CSS variables when the project has no Tailwind. Each component comes with its framework free core (`<name>.core.ts`) and the shared files it imports, nothing to install.

On React Native, `tw.tsx` holds `View`, `Text`, `Pressable`, `TextInput` and `Animated` with className support, `cn()` to merge classes and `useToken()` to read a token as a color. The tokens go at the end of the first `global.css` found (root, `src/`, `app/`, `styles/`, or any CSS file importing Tailwind). With none, it writes `dissolve.css` next to the components: import it from your Tailwind entry.

Running it twice is safe: files and tokens that exist are left alone.

- [Theming](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/theming/)
- [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/cli/

---

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/theming/

# Theming

Twelve tokens, light and dark. Change them once and every component follows, or override one instance with a className.

`init` adds the tokens to your `global.css`. Components take their colors from classes like `bg-dissolve-surface` or `text-dissolve-foreground`, so they follow your palette. On the web, components read the same `--dissolve-*` variables directly, with or without Tailwind.

## Tokens

| Token | Light | Dark | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dissolve-background` | `255 255 255` | `0 0 0` | Screen behind the components |
| `--dissolve-surface` | `242 242 247` | `28 28 30` | Tracks, pads, bubbles, frames |
| `--dissolve-surface-2` | `229 229 234` | `44 44 46` | Raised pills and controls |
| `--dissolve-foreground` | `28 28 30` | `242 242 247` | Text, digits, ink |
| `--dissolve-muted` | `142 142 147` | `152 152 157` | Secondary text, idle icons, placeholders |
| `--dissolve-primary` | `28 28 30` | `242 242 247` | Main buttons, knobs, toasts |
| `--dissolve-primary-foreground` | `255 255 255` | `28 28 30` | Content on primary |
| `--dissolve-success` | `52 199 89` | `48 209 88` | Done and verified states |
| `--dissolve-danger` | `255 59 48` | `255 69 58` | Destructive actions, wrong codes |
| `--dissolve-danger-foreground` | `255 255 255` | `255 255 255` | Content on danger |
| `--dissolve-accent` | `10 132 255` | `10 132 255` | Your own voice notes, highlights |
| `--dissolve-border` | `60 60 67 / 0.12` | `84 84 88 / 0.5` | Hairlines, the signing line |
| `--dissolve-chart-1` | `255 55 135` | `255 79 152` | First chart series, pink |
| `--dissolve-chart-2` | `124 92 255` | `142 114 255` | Second chart series, violet |
| `--dissolve-chart-3` | `255 196 0` | `255 210 51` | Third chart series, yellow |

Each token is also a Tailwind color: `bg-dissolve-primary`, `text-dissolve-muted`, `border-dissolve-border`. Use them in your own screens too.

## Change them

Edit the values in `global.css`. Light values live on `:root`, dark ones in the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block below.

global.css:

```css
/* global.css, after init */
:root {
  --dissolve-primary: rgb(120 72 40);
  --dissolve-primary-foreground: rgb(255 248 240);
  --dissolve-accent: rgb(196 120 60);
}

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --dissolve-primary: rgb(232 200 168);
    --dissolve-primary-foreground: rgb(40 24 12);
  }
}
```

## Dark mode

Nothing to wire: the dark block follows the system color scheme and components switch live. Keep the `:root` plus media query pattern, `light-dark()` does not resolve on native.

## Why @theme inline

The tokens are mapped to Tailwind colors with `@theme inline`. Without `inline`, a class points at a `--color-*` variable that can be resolved once at the root, and on native it keeps the light value. With it, each class reads `var(--dissolve-*)` directly and picks the value of the current color scheme.

global.css:

```css
@layer theme {
  @theme inline {
    --color-dissolve-surface: var(--dissolve-surface);
    /* ... one line per token */
  }
}
```

## Override one instance

Every component takes `className`, plus a className per part: `textClassName`, `knobClassName`, `boxClassName` and so on, listed in its props. Classes are merged with `tailwind-merge`, so yours win over the default of the same kind.

Order.tsx:

```tsx
// Defaults: track bg-dissolve-surface, number text-dissolve-foreground
<SlideToConfirm
  label="Slide to order"
  onConfirm={order}
  className="bg-amber-100"                      // replaces bg-dissolve-surface
/>

<NumberTicker
  value={total}
  textClassName="text-emerald-600 font-bold"    // replaces the color and the weight
/>
```

Some colors are animated or drawn by Skia (OTP boxes, signature ink, waveform). They read the tokens through `useToken()`, so change the token, or edit the file: it is yours.

Your own Skia drawing:

```tsx
import { useToken } from '@/components/dissolve/tw';

const ink = useToken('foreground'); // live color string, light or dark
<Path path={stroke} color={ink} />
```

- [Browse components](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/components/swipe-to-delete/)
- [CLI](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/cli/)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/theming/

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/components/swipe-to-delete/

# SwipeToDelete

**SwipeToDelete** is an animated swipe to delete component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Swipe a row left to delete it: it dissolves, then the list closes up.

A row you swipe left to delete, like Mail or WhatsApp. Past 40 percent, or with a quick flick, the row dissolves, the list closes up behind it, then onDelete runs.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add swipe-to-delete toast --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/swipe-to-delete.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add swipe-to-delete toast --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/swipe-to-delete.json
```

## Usage

SwipeToDelete.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SwipeToDelete } from '@/components/dissolve/swipe-to-delete';
import { useToast } from '@/components/dissolve/toast';

export function Inbox() {
  const [mails, setMails] = useState(MAILS);
  const toast = useToast();

  return mails.map((m) => (
    <SwipeToDelete
      key={m.id}
      rowClassName="rounded-[18px]"
      onDelete={() => {
        setMails((l) => l.filter((x) => x.id !== m.id));
        toast.show({
          title: 'Conversation deleted',
          message: m.from,
          action: { label: 'Undo', onPress: () => restore(m) },
        });
      }}
    >
      <MailRow mail={m} />
    </SwipeToDelete>
  ));
}
```

SwipeToDelete.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SwipeToDelete } from '@/components/dissolve/swipe-to-delete';
import { useToast } from '@/components/dissolve/toast';

export function Inbox() {
  const [mails, setMails] = useState(MAILS);
  const toast = useToast();

  return mails.map((m) => (
    <SwipeToDelete
      key={m.id}
      rowClassName="rounded-[18px]"
      onDelete={() => {
        setMails((l) => l.filter((x) => x.id !== m.id));
        toast.show({
          title: 'Conversation deleted',
          message: m.from,
          action: { label: 'Undo', onPress: () => restore(m) },
        });
      }}
    >
      <MailRow mail={m} />
    </SwipeToDelete>
  ));
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | `required` | The row. It slides with your finger over the delete action. |
| `onDelete` | `() => void` | `required` | Called once the row has dissolved and collapsed: remove the item from your data here. |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Exit used when the row goes. |
| `threshold` | `number` | `0.4` | Fraction of the row width to drag before release deletes. A flick faster than 900 pt/s deletes too. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the pan gesture off. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Outer wrapper (margins, layout). This is the part that collapses. |
| `rowClassName` | `string` | `'overflow-hidden'` | Clipping row. Corner radius goes here (`rounded-2xl`), the action follows it. |
| `actionClassName` | `string` | `'bg-dissolve-danger'` | Delete action revealed behind the row. |

- React: [registry/web/swipe-to-delete.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/swipe-to-delete.tsx) and [registry/web/swipe-to-delete.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/swipe-to-delete.core.ts)

# Toast

**Toast** is an animated toast component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Toasts that arrive in grains and leave as dust, with an optional Undo action.

Toasts that arrive in grains and leave as dust. A provider holds the stack at the top of the screen, three at most: over the limit the oldest one leaves as dust instead of vanishing.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add toast --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/toast.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add toast --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/toast.json
```

## Usage

Toast.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@/components/dissolve/toast';

// app/_layout.tsx, inside <DissolveProvider>
<ToastProvider top={insets.top + 8}>
  <Stack />
</ToastProvider>

// any screen
const toast = useToast();

toast.show({ title: 'Changes saved', tone: 'success' });
toast.show({
  title: 'Photo deleted',
  message: 'Lisbon, 3 years ago',
  action: { label: 'Undo', onPress: restore },
});
toast.show({ title: 'Payment declined', message: 'Try another card', tone: 'error', exit: 'pixel' });
```

Toast.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@/components/dissolve/toast';

// app/layout.tsx
<ToastProvider top={8}>
  {children}
</ToastProvider>

// any screen
const toast = useToast();

toast.show({ title: 'Changes saved', tone: 'success' });
toast.show({
  title: 'Photo deleted',
  message: 'Lisbon, 3 years ago',
  action: { label: 'Undo', onPress: restore },
});
toast.show({ title: 'Payment declined', message: 'Try another card', tone: 'error', exit: 'pixel' });
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `required` | First line, one line. |
| `message` | `string` |  | Second line, up to two lines. |
| `tone` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'error'` | `'default'` | Color of the dot: gray, green or red. |
| `action` | `{ label, onPress }` |  | A single action, typically Undo. The toast leaves after it runs. |
| `duration` | `number` | `3200` | Time on screen before it leaves on its own, ms. 0 keeps it until tapped. |
| `enter` | `VariantName` | `'gather'` | Entrance. |
| `exit` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Exit. |
| `<ToastProvider top>` | `number` | `56` | Distance from the top of the screen. |
| `<ToastProvider max>` | `number` | `3` | Toasts on screen at once. |
| `<ToastProvider className>` | `string` | `'left-3 right-3 gap-2'` | Stack: side insets, gap. |
| `<ToastProvider cardClassName>` | `string` | `'bg-dissolve-primary rounded-[18px]'` | Every card: background, radius, padding. |

# GlossyButton

**GlossyButton** is an animated glossy button component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Tactile pill lit from the inside: gradient stroke, inner light and ring, presses down on a crisp spring.

A pill button with a slightly 3D look, built from one recipe: a 1 pt inside stroke as a white gradient lit from the top, a soft black drop shadow, a white inner shadow and a thin outer ring in the fill color. Pressed, it scales to 0.97 on a crisp spring while the inner light dims, with a light haptic. Every layer is a prop, tune them here and copy the JSX.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add glossy-button --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/glossy-button.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add glossy-button --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/glossy-button.json
```

## Usage

GlossyButton.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { GlossyButton } from '@/components/dissolve/glossy-button';

<GlossyButton onPress={start}>Get started</GlossyButton>

<GlossyButton
  icon={({ color, size }) => <SymbolView name="plus" tintColor={color} size={size} />}
  onPress={create}
>
  New project
</GlossyButton>

<GlossyButton color="#E5484D" radius={14} size="lg" onPress={remove}>
  Delete
</GlossyButton>
```

GlossyButton.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { GlossyButton } from '@/components/dissolve/glossy-button';

<GlossyButton onPress={start}>Get started</GlossyButton>

<GlossyButton
  icon={({ color, size }) => <Icon name="plus" color={color} size={size} />}
  onPress={create}
>
  New project
</GlossyButton>

<GlossyButton color="#E5484D" radius={14} size="lg" onPress={remove}>
  Delete
</GlossyButton>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children / label` | `ReactNode / string` |  | The label. A string is styled with labelColor, any other node renders as is. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode \| ({ color, size }) => ReactNode` |  | Leading icon. The function form gets the label color and the icon size. |
| `onPress` | `() => void` |  | Called on release. |
| `color` | `string` | `'#296FF0'` | Fill, also the color of the outer ring. |
| `labelColor` | `string` | `'#FFFFFF'` | Label and icon color. |
| `radius` | `number` | `999` | Corner radius, capped at half the height (a pill). |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Height 36, 44 or 52, with matching padding and type. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretches to the full width of the parent. |
| `strokeOpacity` | `number` | `0.4` | Top opacity of the 1 pt white gradient stroke, fading to 0 at the bottom. |
| `innerOpacity / innerBlur / innerSpread` | `number` | `0.24 / 6 / 2` | White inner shadow. Dims while pressed. |
| `shadowOpacity / shadowY / shadowBlur` | `number` | `0.2 / 3 / 6` | Black drop shadow. |
| `ringSpread` | `number` | `1` | Outer ring in the fill color, no blur. 0 removes it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Half opacity, no press, no haptic. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on press in. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Outer classes (margins, alignment, width...). |
| `labelClassName` | `string` |  | Label classes (weight, tracking...). |

# LikeButton

**LikeButton** is an animated like button component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Heart that pops with sparks on like and snaps into grains on unlike.

Like: the heart pops and ten sparks burst around it. Unlike: the filled heart snaps away into grains from its center and the outline is back.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add like-button --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/like-button.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add like-button --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/like-button.json
```

## Usage

LikeButton.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { LikeButton } from '@/components/dissolve/like-button';

export function PostActions() {
  const [liked, setLiked] = useState(false);
  const [likes, setLikes] = useState(128);

  return (
    <LikeButton
      liked={liked}
      count={likes}
      onChange={(v) => {
        setLiked(v);
        setLikes((n) => n + (v ? 1 : -1));
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

LikeButton.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { LikeButton } from '@/components/dissolve/like-button';

export function PostActions() {
  const [liked, setLiked] = useState(false);
  const [likes, setLikes] = useState(128);

  return (
    <LikeButton
      liked={liked}
      count={likes}
      onChange={(v) => {
        setLiked(v);
        setLikes((n) => n + (v ? 1 : -1));
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `liked` | `boolean` | `required` | Controlled state. |
| `onChange` | `(liked: boolean) => void` | `required` | Called with true right away on like, with false once the heart has snapped away. |
| `size` | `number` | `26` | Heart size in points. |
| `color` | `string` | `'#FF2D55'` | Filled heart and counter when liked. |
| `idleColor` | `string` | `muted token` | Outline and counter when not liked. |
| `count` | `number` |  | Optional counter shown next to the heart. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on like, the snap ticks on unlike. |
| `className` | `string` | `'flex-row items-center gap-1.5'` | Row: gap, padding, margins. |
| `countClassName` | `string` | `'text-[15px] font-semibold'` | Counter text: size, weight. |

- React: [registry/web/like-button.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/like-button.tsx) and [registry/web/like-button.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/like-button.core.ts)

# MorphButton

**MorphButton** is an animated morph button component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Dynamic Island style pill that folds into a loader, then opens as the done state.

A button that morphs like the Dynamic Island: the pill folds into a round loader, then opens back up as the done state. Crisp shape, a critically damped spring, content that cross-fades and scales.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh

```

```sh

```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh

```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/morph-button.json
```

## Usage

MorphButton.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { MorphButton } from '@/components/dissolve/morph-button';

<MorphButton
  label="Pay 42 €"
  doneLabel="Paid"

import { MorphButton } from '@/components/dissolve/morph-button';

  doneLabel="Paid"

```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `required` | Idle label. |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | `'Done'` | Label next to the check once the promise resolves. |
| `onPress` | `() => Promise \| void` | `required` | Runs on press. The button stays in its loading state until the promise settles; a rejection goes back to idle. |
| `height` | `number` | `52` | Pill height, also the loader diameter. |
| `resetAfter` | `number` | `1800` | Time spent on the done state before going back, ms. 0 stays done. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on press, success when done. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Outer box (width, margins). The pill is centered inside it. |
| `labelClassName` | `string` | `'text-base font-semibold text-dissolve-primary-foreground'` | Label and done label: size, weight, color. The pill reads the primary and success tokens. |

## Source

- React Native: [registry/morph-button.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/morph-button.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/morph-button.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/morph-button.tsx) and [registry/web/morph-button.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/morph-button.core.ts)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/components/morph-button/

# SplitButton

**SplitButton** is an animated split button component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Splits in two like a drop of liquid metal, Cancel and Confirm halves.

A button that divides in the middle like a drop of liquid metal: the two halves pull apart, a neck between them thins into a waist, then snaps. Cancel fuses them back. Vector edges, no blur, so it stays crisp.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add split-button --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/split-button.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add split-button --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/split-button.json
```

## Usage

SplitButton.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { SplitButton } from '@/components/dissolve/split-button';
import { useToast } from '@/components/dissolve/toast';

const toast = useToast();

<SplitButton
  label="Delete project"
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  onConfirm={() => toast.show({ title: 'Project deleted', tone: 'error' })}
/>
```

SplitButton.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { SplitButton } from '@/components/dissolve/split-button';
import { useToast } from '@/components/dissolve/toast';

const toast = useToast();

<SplitButton
  label="Delete project"
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  onConfirm={() => toast.show({ title: 'Project deleted', tone: 'error' })}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `required` | Label of the whole button. |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | `'Cancel'` | Left half once split. |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` | `'Confirm'` | Right half once split. |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void` | `required` | Runs on the right half, then the halves fuse back. |
| `height` | `number` | `52` | Button height. |
| `gap` | `number` | `28` | Space between the two halves once split. The neck snaps at 80 percent of it. |
| `duration` | `number` | `620` | Split duration, ms. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Selection tick on taps, warning on confirm. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Root: margins, width. The drop reads the danger tokens, the Cancel half surface-2. |
| `labelClassName` | `string` | `'text-base font-semibold'` | Every label: size, weight. |
| `cancelLabelClassName` | `string` | `'text-dissolve-foreground'` | Cancel label, its color. |

# GooeyMenu

**GooeyMenu** is an animated gooey menu component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Floating button whose actions pour out as gooey drops.

A floating button whose actions pour out of it as drops along an arc and melt back in when it closes. Place it absolutely: it reserves room for the arc above and to the left of the button.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add gooey-menu --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/gooey-menu.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add gooey-menu --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/gooey-menu.json
```

## Usage

GooeyMenu.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { GooeyMenu } from '@/components/dissolve/gooey-menu';

<GooeyMenu
  className="absolute bottom-2 right-2"
  items={[
    { icon: <Icon name="camera" />, label: 'Camera', onPress: openCamera },
    { icon: <Icon name="photo" />, label: 'Photo', onPress: openLibrary },
    { icon: <Icon name="mic" />, label: 'Voice', onPress: record },
  ]}
/>
```

GooeyMenu.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { GooeyMenu } from '@/components/dissolve/gooey-menu';

<GooeyMenu
  className="absolute bottom-2 right-2"
  items={[
    { icon: <Icon name="camera" />, label: 'Camera', onPress: openCamera },
    { icon: <Icon name="photo" />, label: 'Photo', onPress: openLibrary },
    { icon: <Icon name="mic" />, label: 'Voice', onPress: record },
  ]}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `GooeyMenuItem[]` | `required` | `{ icon, onPress, label? }`. The menu closes after an action runs. |
| `size` | `number` | `56` | Diameter of the main button. Actions are 82 percent of it. |
| `distance` | `number` | `92` | Distance from the main button to the actions. |
| `startAngle` | `number` | `-90` | Arc start in degrees, 0 = right, -90 = up. |
| `endAngle` | `number` | `-180` | Arc end in degrees, -180 = left. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on toggle. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Root: position it here. Button and drops read the primary token. |
| `iconClassName` | `string` | `'bg-dissolve-primary-foreground'` | The two bars of the plus, their color. |

# SlideToConfirm

**SlideToConfirm** is an animated slide to confirm component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Slide to pay or confirm, shimmer label, loader, done state.

Slide to pay or confirm, like Apple Pay or power off. A light shimmer runs across the label, the track fills behind the knob, and past the threshold it locks, loads, then confirms.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add slide-to-confirm --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/slide-to-confirm.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add slide-to-confirm --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/slide-to-confirm.json
```

## Usage

SlideToConfirm.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { SlideToConfirm } from '@/components/dissolve/slide-to-confirm';

<SlideToConfirm
  label="Slide to pay 42 €"
  doneLabel="Paid"
  onConfirm={() => pay(order)} // the knob shows a loader until the promise settles
/>
```

SlideToConfirm.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { SlideToConfirm } from '@/components/dissolve/slide-to-confirm';

<SlideToConfirm
  label="Slide to pay 42 €"
  doneLabel="Paid"
  onConfirm={() => pay(order)} // the knob shows a loader until the promise settles
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `required` | Label on the track, with a shimmer running across it. |
| `onConfirm` | `() => Promise \| void` | `required` | Runs once the knob reaches the end. The knob shows a loader until the promise settles; a rejection goes back to idle. |
| `doneLabel` | `string` | `'Done'` | Label once confirmed. |
| `height` | `number` | `60` | Track height. The knob is 10 points smaller. |
| `threshold` | `number` | `0.88` | Fraction of the track to reach before release confirms. A flick past halfway confirms too. |
| `resetAfter` | `number` | `1600` | Time on the done state before the slider resets, ms. 0 stays done. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Medium impact on lock, success when done. |
| `className` | `string` | `'rounded-full bg-dissolve-surface'` | Track: background, radius, margins. Fill, label and done state read the primary, muted and success tokens. |
| `knobClassName` | `string` | `'rounded-full shadow-md'` | Knob: shadow, extra layout. Its color is animated from the primary token. |

- React: [registry/web/slide-to-confirm.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/slide-to-confirm.tsx) and [registry/web/slide-to-confirm.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/slide-to-confirm.core.ts)

# OTPInput

**OTPInput** is an animated OTP input component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. One time code boxes, verify sweep, success tint, shake and dust on reject.

One time code input. A hidden field (SMS autofill, paste) drives the boxes, the active box blinks a calm caret and each digit lands crisply. A full code is checked: the boxes turn green, or the row shakes and the digits blow away as dust before the input clears and asks again.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add otp-input --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/otp-input.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add otp-input --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/otp-input.json
```

## Usage

OTPInput.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { OTPInput } from '@/components/dissolve/otp-input';

<OTPInput
  autoFocus
  onComplete={async (code) => (await api.verify(code)).ok}
/>
```

OTPInput.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { OTPInput } from '@/components/dissolve/otp-input';

<OTPInput
  autoFocus
  onComplete={async (code) => (await api.verify(code)).ok}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `length` | `number` | `6` | Number of digits. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Controlled value. Leave undefined to let the input own its state. |
| `onChange` | `(code: string) => void` |  | Called on every change. |
| `onComplete` | `(code: string) => boolean \| void \| Promise` |  | Runs once every box is filled. True shows the success state, false rejects: the row shakes, the digits turn to dust and the input clears. Nothing leaves the code in place. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Focus on mount. |
| `height` | `number` | `56` | Box height. Box width follows the available space unless boxWidth is set. |
| `boxWidth` | `number` |  | Fixed box width. |
| `gap` | `number` | `8` | Space between boxes. |
| `fontSize` | `number` | `26` | Digit size. |
| `radius` | `number` | `14` | Box corner radius. |
| `blurOnSuccess` | `boolean` | `true` | Close the keyboard once the code is accepted. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Success and error notifications. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Root: margins, width. |
| `boxClassName` | `string` |  | Every box: shadow, extra layout. Box colors are animated from the surface, border, foreground, success and danger tokens. |
| `digitClassName` | `string` | `'font-semibold'` | Digits: weight, family. Their color is animated from the tokens. |

- React: [registry/web/otp-input.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/otp-input.tsx) and [registry/web/otp-input.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/otp-input.core.ts)

# NumberTicker

**NumberTicker** is an animated number ticker component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Rolling digit columns for prices and counters, locale aware.

Animated number for prices, balances and counters. Every digit is a clipped 0 to 9 column that rolls to its new value on a calm iOS curve, right to left with a slight stagger. Added digits open in, removed ones fold out, so the layout never jumps.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add number-ticker --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/number-ticker.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add number-ticker --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/number-ticker.json
```

## Usage

NumberTicker.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { NumberTicker } from '@/components/dissolve/number-ticker';

<NumberTicker
  value={balance}
  decimals={2}
  locale="fr-FR"
  suffix={'\u00A0€'}
  fontSize={44}
/>
```

NumberTicker.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { NumberTicker } from '@/components/dissolve/number-ticker';

<NumberTicker
  value={balance}
  decimals={2}
  locale="fr-FR"
  suffix={'\u00A0€'}
  fontSize={44}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | `required` | The number to show. Digits roll whenever it changes. |
| `decimals` | `number` | `0` | Digits after the decimal separator. |
| `locale` | `string` |  | Picks the separators, e.g. 'fr-FR' gives "1 240,50", 'en-US' "1,240.50". |
| `separator` | `string` |  | Overrides the locale thousands separator. '' turns grouping off. |
| `decimalSeparator` | `string` |  | Overrides the locale decimal separator. |
| `prefix` | `string` |  | Static text before the number, e.g. '$'. |
| `suffix` | `string` |  | Static text after the number, e.g. a no break space and €. |
| `fontSize` | `number` | `34` | Text size. |
| `duration` | `number` | `700` | Roll duration, ms. |
| `stagger` | `number` | `28` | Delay between two columns, right to left, ms. |
| `tabular` | `boolean` | `true` | Tabular figures, so digits never change width. |
| `className` | `string` | `'flex-row items-center self-start'` | Root: margins, alignment. |
| `textClassName` | `string` | `'font-semibold text-dissolve-foreground'` | Number: color, weight, family. |
| `affixClassName` | `string` |  | Prefix and suffix, added on top of the number classes. |

# ReactionPicker

**ReactionPicker** is an animated reaction picker component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. iMessage style reactions: long press, dock magnifier, emoji flies to a badge.

iMessage style reactions. Long press a bubble: it lifts, a pill of emojis grows out of the press point. Slide across and the emoji under the finger magnifies like the Dock. Release on one to pick it, it flies to the bubble corner. Pick the same one again and the badge snaps into grains.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add reaction-picker --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/reaction-picker.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add reaction-picker --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/reaction-picker.json
```

## Usage

ReactionPicker.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ReactionPicker } from '@/components/dissolve/reaction-picker';

export function Message({ text }) {
  const [reaction, setReaction] = useState(null);

  return (
    <ReactionPicker
      selected={reaction}
      onReact={(e) => setReaction(e === reaction ? null : e)}
    >
      <Bubble text={text} />
    </ReactionPicker>
  );
}
```

ReactionPicker.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ReactionPicker } from '@/components/dissolve/reaction-picker';

export function Message({ text }) {
  const [reaction, setReaction] = useState(null);

  return (
    <ReactionPicker
      selected={reaction}
      onReact={(e) => setReaction(e === reaction ? null : e)}
    >
      <Bubble text={text} />
    </ReactionPicker>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | `required` | The bubble. It lifts while the picker is open. |
| `onReact` | `(emoji: string) => void` | `required` | Called with the chosen emoji. Picking the current one again is your cue to remove it. |
| `reactions` | `string[]` | `['❤️', '😂', '😮', '😢', '👍', '🔥']` | Emojis offered in the pill. |
| `selected` | `string \| null` |  | Current reaction, shown as a badge on the bubble corner. |
| `corner` | `'top-left' \| 'top-right'` | `'top-right'` | Corner the badge sits on. Use top-left for your own bubbles. |
| `insets` | `{ top?, bottom? }` | `{ top: 60, bottom: 34 }` | Space kept free at the top and bottom of the window (safe area). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the long press off. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Medium impact on open, a tick per emoji crossed, light impact on pick. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Wrapper: margins, alignment. |
| `pillClassName` | `string` |  | Emoji pill: background, border, shadow. |
| `badgeClassName` | `string` |  | Badge disc, also used by the emoji flying to the bubble. |
| `backdropClassName` | `string` | `transparent` | Layer over the screen while the picker is open, e.g. `bg-black/20` to dim. |

## Source

- React Native: [registry/reaction-picker.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/reaction-picker.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/reaction-picker.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/reaction-picker.tsx) and [registry/web/reaction-picker.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/reaction-picker.core.ts)

# VoiceNote

**VoiceNote** is an animated voice note component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Voice message bubble: play, scrub the waveform with ticks, unsend as dust.

A voice message bubble. Play and pause, the played part of the waveform takes the ink, drag along it to seek. Long press to unsend: the bubble blows away as dust. No audio dependency, playback is a timer you hook to your player.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add voice-note --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/voice-note.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add voice-note --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/voice-note.json
```

## Usage

VoiceNote.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { VoiceNote } from '@/components/dissolve/voice-note';

<VoiceNote
  mine
  duration={9}
  seed="msg-42"
  onPlay={() => player.play()}
  onPause={() => player.pause()}
  onUnsend={() => remove(id)}
/>
```

VoiceNote.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { VoiceNote } from '@/components/dissolve/voice-note';

<VoiceNote
  mine
  duration={9}
  seed="msg-42"
  onPlay={() => player.play()}
  onPause={() => player.pause()}
  onUnsend={() => remove(id)}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `duration` | `number` | `required` | Length of the note in seconds. Playback is simulated with a timer. |
| `levels` | `number[]` |  | Loudness per sample, 0 to 1. Resampled to the number of bars that fit. |
| `seed` | `number \| string` | `1` | Generates a deterministic, speech like waveform when levels is not given. |
| `mine` | `boolean` | `false` | Your own message: accent bubble with white content. Otherwise a surface bubble. |
| `width` | `number` | `248` | Bubble width. |
| `onPlay / onPause / onEnd` | `() => void` |  | Hook your audio player here. |
| `onUnsend` | `() => void` |  | Called once the bubble has dissolved: remove it from your data here. |
| `unsent` | `boolean` | `false` | Flip to true to unsend from outside (a menu, a swipe). |
| `unsendOnLongPress` | `boolean` | `true with onUnsend` | Long press the bubble (480 ms) to unsend. |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Exit used when the note is unsent. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on play, a tick per bar while seeking. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Bubble: background, radius, padding. |
| `buttonClassName` | `string` |  | Play and pause button. |
| `labelClassName` | `string` |  | Time label. |

# SignaturePad

**SignaturePad** is an animated signature pad component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Variable width Skia signature, undo, clear into dust, PNG export.

Sign with your finger or a mouse. Ink is drawn as variable width strokes, thick when slow and thin when fast, with tapered ends, on a signing line whose placeholder fades as you start. Undo removes the last stroke, Clear turns the signature into dust and leaves the paper.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add signature-pad --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/signature-pad.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add signature-pad --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/signature-pad.json
```

## Usage

SignaturePad.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { SignaturePad, type SignaturePadHandle } from '@/components/dissolve/signature-pad';

export function Sign() {
  const pad = useRef<SignaturePadHandle>(null);

  return (
    <SignaturePad
      ref={pad}
      placeholder="Sign here"
      onChange={setSigned}
      onSave={({ base64 }) => upload(base64)}
    />
  );
}

// pad.current?.save(), pad.current?.clear() dissolves the ink
```

SignaturePad.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { SignaturePad, type SignaturePadHandle } from '@/components/dissolve/signature-pad';

export function Sign() {
  const pad = useRef<SignaturePadHandle>(null);

  return (
    <SignaturePad
      ref={pad}
      placeholder="Sign here"
      onChange={setSigned}
      onSave={({ base64 }) => upload(base64)}
    />
  );
}

// pad.current?.save(), pad.current?.clear() dissolves the ink
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strokeColor` | `string` | `foreground token` | Ink color, also used for the exported PNG. |
| `strokeWidth` | `number` | `3.2` | Base nib width. Slow strokes get thicker, fast ones thinner. |
| `onChange` | `(hasSignature: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the pad goes from empty to signed and back. |
| `onSave` | `(signature: SignatureExport) => void` |  | Receives the image, a base64 PNG and its size, from save(). |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `'Sign here'` | Shown above the line, fades once you start. |
| `height` | `number` | `200` | Pad height. |
| `exportBackground` | `string` | `transparent` | Background of the exported PNG. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `true` | Built in Undo and Clear pills. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Selection tick on undo, dust haptics on clear. |
| `className` | `string` | `'rounded-[20px] bg-dissolve-surface'` | Pad: background, radius, border. |
| `guideClassName` | `string` | `'bg-dissolve-border'` | Signing line. |
| `placeholderClassName` | `string` | `'text-dissolve-muted'` | Placeholder and x mark. |
| `controlClassName` | `string` | `'rounded-full bg-dissolve-surface-2'` | Undo and Clear pills. |
| `ref` | `Ref<SignaturePadHandle>` |  | `undo()`, `clear()`, `isEmpty()`, `toImage()`, `save()`. |

# CardStack

**CardStack** is an animated card stack component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Wallet style card stack: tap to focus, drag down to put back, swipe to cycle.

A Wallet style stack. Cards overlap and show their top strip; tap one and it comes forward while the others slide down and compress under it. Drag the focused card down to put it back, swipe it sideways to go to the next one. One calm curve, no bounce, and a fixed height so nothing around it relayouts.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add card-stack --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/card-stack.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add card-stack --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/card-stack.json
```

## Usage

CardStack.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { CardStack } from '@/components/dissolve/card-stack';

<CardStack
  items={cards}
  keyExtractor={(c) => c.id}
  renderCard={(c) => <PaymentCard card={c} />}
  onFocus={setActive}
/>
```

CardStack.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { CardStack } from '@/components/dissolve/card-stack';

<CardStack
  items={cards}
  keyExtractor={(c) => c.id}
  renderCard={(c) => <PaymentCard card={c} />}
  onFocus={setActive}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `T[]` | `required` | The cards, top of the stack first. |
| `renderCard` | `(item: T, index: number) => ReactNode` | `required` | Renders one card face. It is clipped to the card radius. |
| `cardHeight` | `number` | `width / 1.586` | Card height. The default is the ISO payment card ratio. |
| `peek` | `number` | `60` | Visible strip of each card in the stack. |
| `onFocus` | `(index: number \| null) => void` |  | Called with the focused index, or null when back to the stack. |
| `keyExtractor` | `(item: T, index: number) => string` |  | Stable keys for the cards. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on focus, soft on restack, a tick when cycling. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Container: margins, padding. |
| `cardClassName` | `string` | `'rounded-[20px]' + shadow` | Card chrome: corner radius and shadow. Replaces the default, a soft shadow cast upward on the card behind. |

# BeforeAfter

**BeforeAfter** is an animated before after component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Before / after image comparison with a draggable divider and haptic ticks.

Compare two versions of an image. Drag the round handle, or anywhere on the frame, or tap to send the divider there. The before layer is clipped to the left of the divider without relayout, and the pills fade as the divider reaches them.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add before-after --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/before-after.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add before-after --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/before-after.json
```

## Usage

BeforeAfter.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { Image } from 'expo-image';
import { BeforeAfter } from '@/components/dissolve/before-after';

<BeforeAfter
  height={320}
  initial={0.42}
  afterLabel="Vivid"
  renderBefore={({ width, height }) => <Image source={raw} style={{ width, height }} />}
  renderAfter={({ width, height }) => <Image source={edited} style={{ width, height }} />}
/>
```

BeforeAfter.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { BeforeAfter } from '@/components/dissolve/before-after';

<BeforeAfter
  height={320}
  initial={0.42}
  afterLabel="Vivid"
  renderBefore={({ width, height }) => <img src={raw} style={{ width, height }} />}
  renderAfter={({ width, height }) => <img src={edited} style={{ width, height }} />}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before / after` | `ReactNode` |  | The two versions, left and right of the divider. |
| `renderBefore / renderAfter` | `(size) => ReactNode` |  | Render props given the frame size, for images that need explicit dimensions. |
| `initial` | `number` | `0.5` | Initial divider position, 0 (all after) to 1 (all before). |
| `height` | `number` | `320` | Frame height. |
| `beforeLabel` | `string` | `'Before'` | Left pill. |
| `afterLabel` | `string` | `'After'` | Right pill. |
| `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the two pills. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Divider position (0..1) when a drag or a tap settles. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | A tick at the middle, a light impact at both edges. |
| `className` | `string` | `'rounded-[20px] bg-dissolve-surface-2'` | Frame: radius, placeholder background, margins. |
| `handleClassName` | `string` |  | Round handle. |
| `dividerClassName` | `string` |  | Divider line. |
| `pillClassName` | `string` |  | Before and After pills. |
| `pillTextClassName` | `string` | `'text-[12px] font-semibold text-white'` | Pill labels. |
