# ThinkingOrb

**ThinkingOrb** is an animated thinking orb component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. A sphere of dots that shows what an AI agent is doing: thinking, searching, listening, done.

An agent status indicator made of 180 dots. Idle, it breathes as a sphere; thinking, the dots split into three tilted rings; searching, the sphere flattens into a disc swept by a radar arc; listening, it pulses with the voice level; done, the dots fly into a checkmark; error, they fall and reform. Every state change moves each dot from where it is to its new place on the calm curve, staggered, never instant. With interactive on, dots flee the finger and spring back.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add thinking-orb --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/thinking-orb.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add thinking-orb --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/thinking-orb.json
```

## Usage

ThinkingOrb.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { ThinkingOrb } from '@/components/dissolve/thinking-orb';

<ThinkingOrb
  state={agent.status} // 'idle' | 'thinking' | 'searching' | 'listening' | 'done' | 'error'
  size={96}
  level={micLevel}
  interactive
/>
```

ThinkingOrb.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { ThinkingOrb } from '@/components/dissolve/thinking-orb';

<ThinkingOrb
  state={agent.status} // 'idle' | 'thinking' | 'searching' | 'listening' | 'done' | 'error'
  size={96}
  level={micLevel} // a number, or an object whose value is read every frame
  interactive
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `'idle' \| 'thinking' \| 'searching' \| 'listening' \| 'done' \| 'error'` | `'idle'` | What the agent is doing. Each change moves every dot to its new place in 600 ms, staggered. |
| `size` | `number` | `64` | Diameter of the orb. |
| `dots` | `number` | `180` | Number of dots. |
| `dotSize` | `number` | `2.5` | Dot diameter in points. |
| `level` | `SharedValue<number>` |  | Voice level 0 to 1 that drives the listening pulse. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `false` | Dots flee the finger within 40 pt and spring back. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on done, warning on error. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes of the container. Dots use the foreground token, done the success token, error the danger token. |

- React: [registry/web/thinking-orb.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/thinking-orb.tsx) and [registry/web/thinking-orb.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/thinking-orb.core.ts)

# ImageReveal

**ImageReveal** is an animated image reveal component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Image generation loader: a thinking mosaic that resolves coarse to fine, then settles in grains.

A loader for generated images. While pending, a 12 by 12 mosaic pulses with a slow diagonal wave. When the image arrives, it resolves from 8 to 128 cells in 1.4 s on a smoothstep, one even step per doubling, each cell switching to the real color past its own random threshold, then the finest mosaic crossfades into the sharp image in 180 ms. On error, the mosaic freezes, tints red and leaves as dust. The mosaic is one shader, no view per cell.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add image-reveal --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/image-reveal.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add image-reveal --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/image-reveal.json
```

## Usage

ImageReveal.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { ImageReveal } from '@/components/dissolve/image-reveal';

<ImageReveal
  src={result?.uri}
  status={failed ? 'error' : result ? 'ready' : 'pending'}
  onRevealed={() => setShowActions(true)}
  onDismissed={retry}
  className="rounded-[20px]"
/>
```

ImageReveal.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { ImageReveal } from '@/components/dissolve/image-reveal';

<ImageReveal
  src={result?.uri}
  status={failed ? 'error' : result ? 'ready' : 'pending'}
  onRevealed={() => setShowActions(true)}
  onDismissed={retry}
  className="rounded-[20px]"
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `DataSourceParam` |  | The generated image (require(...) or a uri). Reveals once loaded and status is ready. |
| `status` | `'pending' \| 'ready' \| 'error'` | `src ? 'ready' : 'pending'` | Pending shows the thinking mosaic, error sends it away as dust. |
| `duration` | `number` | `1400` | Coarse to fine resolve, in ms. A 180 ms crossfade to the sharp image follows. |
| `cells` | `number` | `160` | Finest mosaic across the width before the sharp image (8, 16, 32, 64, 128). |
| `aspectRatio` | `number` | `1` | Width / height of the frame. |
| `onRevealed` | `() => void` |  | Called once the sharp image is fully shown. |
| `onDismissed` | `() => void` |  | Error: called once the mosaic has left as dust. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | A tick at each resolution doubling, success at the end. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes of the frame: size, radius. |

## Source

- React Native: [registry/image-reveal.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/image-reveal.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/image-reveal.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/image-reveal.tsx) and [registry/web/image-reveal.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/image-reveal.core.ts)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/components/image-reveal/

# SweepTransition

**SweepTransition** is an animated sweep transition component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. A crisp liquid band sweeps across a view and leaves the new state behind it.

Wrap any view and call run() with your state change. The current view is captured, the new state mounts under it, and a 28 pt band sweeps across the capture, bending what it passes with a light refraction, a hint of RGB split and a 1 pt accent rim. Vertical, horizontal, or a circle growing from a touch point. cancel() sends the band back and restores the old state. No blur.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add sweep-transition --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/sweep-transition.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add sweep-transition --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/sweep-transition.json
```

## Usage

SweepTransition.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { SweepTransition, type SweepTransitionHandle } from '@/components/dissolve/sweep-transition';

const sweep = useRef<SweepTransitionHandle>(null);

<SweepTransition ref={sweep} mode="vertical" className="rounded-3xl">
  <PlanCard plan={plan} />
</SweepTransition>

sweep.current?.run(() => setPlan('pro'), { revert: () => setPlan('free') });
```

SweepTransition.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { SweepTransition, type SweepTransitionHandle } from '@/components/dissolve/sweep-transition';

const sweep = useRef<SweepTransitionHandle>(null);

<SweepTransition ref={sweep} mode="vertical" className="rounded-3xl">
  <PlanCard plan={plan} />
</SweepTransition>

sweep.current?.run(() => setPlan('pro'), { revert: () => setPlan('free') });
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'radial'` | `'vertical'` | Bottom to top, left to right, or a circle from the origin. |
| `duration` | `number` | `720` | Sweep length in ms, calm curve. |
| `bandWidth` | `number` | `28` | Width of the refractive band. |
| `ref.run` | `(apply, { origin?, mode?, revert? }) => Promise<void>` |  | Captures the view, runs apply under the capture, then sweeps it away. origin is the radial center in local points. |
| `ref.cancel` | `() => void` |  | Sends the front back in 300 ms, then calls the run revert to put the old state back. |
| `ref.running` | `() => boolean` |  | True while a sweep is on screen. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light at start, soft when the front passes half. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Classes of the wrapper. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | `required` | The view that changes. |

## Source

- React Native: [registry/sweep-transition.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/sweep-transition.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/sweep-transition.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/sweep-transition.tsx) and [registry/web/sweep-transition.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/sweep-transition.core.ts)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/components/sweep-transition/

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/components/upload-tile/

# UploadTile

**UploadTile** is an animated upload tile component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Attachment that assembles from grains, fills a progress ring, rejected files leave as dust.

An attachment tile for chat composers. The upload progress is the tile itself: from 0 to 1, its grains land one by one, a front running left to right, and at 1 the tile is whole. Only then the remove cross fades in. No ring, no badge. A file over maxSize, or an upload that rejects, completes, shakes three times, turns red and leaves as dust while the row closes up. Tap the tile during the upload to abort: the grains that have landed snap away from your finger. No picker dependency, you pass the files.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add upload-tile --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/upload-tile.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add upload-tile --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/upload-tile.json
```

## Usage

UploadTile.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { UploadTray } from '@/components/dissolve/upload-tile';

<UploadTray
  files={files}
  upload={(file, onProgress, signal) => api.upload(file, { onProgress, signal })}
  maxSize={25 * 1024 * 1024}
  onAdd={pickFiles}
  onRemove={(file) => setFiles((all) => all.filter((f) => f.id !== file.id))}
/>
```

UploadTile.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { UploadTray } from '@/components/dissolve/upload-tile';

<UploadTray
  files={files}
  upload={(file, onProgress, signal) => api.upload(file, { onProgress, signal })}
  maxSize={25 * 1024 * 1024}
  onAdd={pickFiles}
  onRemove={(file) => setFiles((all) => all.filter((f) => f.id !== file.id))}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `{ id?, name, size, uri?, source? }` | `required` | The file. An image uri or source shows as a thumbnail, anything else as a file icon, name and size. |
| `upload` | `(file, onProgress, signal) => Promise<void>` | `required` | Your upload. Report progress 0 to 1: it drives how many grains have landed. Stop when the signal aborts (a tap on the tile aborts it), reject to show the error state. |
| `maxSize` | `number` |  | Bytes. A bigger file is rejected without starting the upload. |
| `size` | `number` | `72` | Tile side. 6 pt of room are kept around it for the cross and the grains. |
| `spacing` | `number` | `0` | Space after the tile in a row. It closes up with the tile. |
| `onDone` | `(file) => void` |  | Called once the upload resolved and the tile is whole, as the cross appears. |
| `onRemove` | `(file, reason: 'rejected' \| 'cancelled' \| 'removed') => void` |  | Called once the tile has gone and its space has closed: drop the file here. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Success when whole, error on reject, light impact on cancel and remove. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Outer wrapper classes (margins). |
| `tileClassName` | `string` |  | Tile classes (background, radius). |

## Source

- React Native: [registry/upload-tile.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/upload-tile.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/upload-tile.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/upload-tile.tsx) and [registry/web/upload-tile.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/upload-tile.core.ts)

# TaskCheck

**TaskCheck** is an animated task check component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Checkbox that draws its check and strikes the label, then the task moves away or dissolves.

A to do row. Tap it: the box fills with a small spring, the check draws in 220 ms, the strike runs across each real line of text and the label goes muted. After a short delay the task moves to Done, or dissolves into dust from the left and the list closes up. Tap again before the delay to undo.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add task-check --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/task-check.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add task-check --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/task-check.json
```

## Usage

TaskCheck.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { TaskCheck } from '@/components/dissolve/task-check';

<TaskCheck
  label={task.title}
  checked={task.done}
  onCheckedChange={(done) => update(task.id, { done })}
  after="move"
  onSettled={() => moveToDone(task.id)}
/>
```

TaskCheck.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { TaskCheck } from '@/components/dissolve/task-check';

<TaskCheck
  label={task.title}
  checked={task.done}
  onCheckedChange={(done) => update(task.id, { done })}
  after="move"
  onSettled={() => moveToDone(task.id)}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `required` | The task. The strike follows each line it wraps to. |
| `checked` | `boolean` | `required` | Checked state. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | `required` | Called on tap. |
| `after` | `'stay' \| 'move' \| 'dissolve'` | `'stay'` | Once checked: nothing, onSettled so you move it to Done, or dust from the left, the gap closes, then onSettled. |
| `settleDelay` | `number` | `900` | Pause before the task settles. A tap within it undoes. |
| `onSettled` | `() => void` |  | Called when the task settles: move it, or drop it after the dust. |
| `boxSize` | `number` | `24` | Checkbox side. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the tap off. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Light impact on check. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Outer wrapper classes (margins, separators). This is the part that closes up. |
| `rowClassName` | `string` |  | Row classes (padding, gap). |
| `labelClassName` | `string` |  | Label classes (size, weight). The color is animated from the tokens. |

- React: [registry/web/task-check.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/task-check.tsx) and [registry/web/task-check.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/task-check.core.ts)

# QuantityStepper

**QuantityStepper** is an animated quantity stepper component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Minus and plus with rolling digits and an accelerating long press; at 1 it turns into a trash.

A minus and plus stepper with rolling digits. A tap steps once; hold a button and it repeats from 380 ms down to 60 ms over 1.5 s, the digits rolling like an odometer and always in sync. At the minimum the minus turns into a trash, armed once its morph is done so a fast double tap never removes the row; tap it and the whole row falls away as sand. At the maximum the pill shakes.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add quantity-stepper --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/quantity-stepper.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add quantity-stepper --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/quantity-stepper.json
```

## Usage

QuantityStepper.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { QuantityStepper } from '@/components/dissolve/quantity-stepper';

const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();

<View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>
  <QuantityStepper
    value={qty}
    onChange={setQty}
    onRemove={async () => {
      await dissolve({ preset: 'sand' });
      removeFromCart(item.id);
    }}
  />
</View>
```

QuantityStepper.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { QuantityStepper } from '@/components/dissolve/quantity-stepper';

<QuantityStepper
  value={qty}
  onChange={setQty}
  onRemove={() => removeFromCart(item.id)}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | `required` | The quantity. Digits roll whenever it changes. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number) => void` | `required` | Called on every step: once per tap (on release), then at 380 ms on hold, accelerating to 60 ms. |
| `min` | `number` | `1` | Lowest value. With onRemove the minus turns into a trash there. |
| `max` | `number` | `99` | Highest value. Going past it shakes the pill. |
| `onRemove` | `() => void` |  | When set, the minus becomes a trash at the minimum and calls this on tap (ignored for 320 ms after reaching it). Dissolve your row here. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Pill height, 30 or 36. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | A tick per step, medium on remove, warning at max. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Pill classes (background, radius, margins...). |
| `textClassName` | `string` |  | Count classes (weight, color...). |

## Source

- React Native: [registry/quantity-stepper.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/quantity-stepper.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/quantity-stepper.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/quantity-stepper.tsx) and [registry/web/quantity-stepper.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/quantity-stepper.core.ts)

# RulerPicker

**RulerPicker** is an animated ruler picker component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Horizontal ruler with momentum, rolling value and a haptic tick per graduation.

A horizontal ruler you drag under a center needle: 1:1 pan, momentum, then a calm snap on the nearest step. The value rolls above it. Graduations near the needle stretch with speed, and a haptic tick lands on every step.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:


```sh

```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/ruler-picker.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add ruler-picker --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/ruler-picker.json
```

## Usage

RulerPicker.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { RulerPicker } from '@/components/dissolve/ruler-picker';

<RulerPicker
  value={kg}
  onChange={setKg}
  min={30}
  max={200}
  step={0.1}
  unit="kg"
/>
```

RulerPicker.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { RulerPicker } from '@/components/dissolve/ruler-picker';

<RulerPicker
  value={kg}
  onChange={setKg}
  min={30}
  max={200}
  step={0.1}
  unit="kg"
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | `required` | Current value. An outside change glides the ruler to it. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called once the ruler is at rest on a new value. |
| `onChanging` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called on every step crossed while dragging or gliding. |
| `min / max` | `number` | `required` | Bounds. Past them the ruler follows with a 0.3 rubber band. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | Value between two graduations. |
| `majorEvery` | `number` | `10` | A labelled major graduation every N steps. |
| `unit` | `string` |  | Unit next to the value, e.g. 'kg'. |
| `format` | `(value: number) => string` |  | Formats the labels and the accessibility value. |
| `tickSpacing` | `number` | `10` | Distance between two graduations, pt. |
| `height` | `number` | `76` | Ruler height. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the rolling value above the ruler. |
| `fontSize` | `number` | `56` | Value size. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | A tick per step, light on majors, rigid at the bounds. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Root classes (margins, width...). |
| `valueClassName` | `string` |  | Value classes, passed to NumberTicker. |

# BarChart

**BarChart** is an animated bar chart component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Bar chart you scrub with a finger, sliding bubble, bars regrow on period change.

A bar chart built from small round dots, a slightly jittered grid with a rounded top per bar. The dots fly in and assemble the bars with a short stagger. Scrub with a finger: the bar under it stays lit while the others step back, a bubble with the value slides along, and the dots near the finger scatter away, then spring back. New data sends the dots falling from the old bars and gathers them into the new ones. Stacked series use the chart tokens: pink, violet and yellow.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add bar-chart --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/bar-chart.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add bar-chart --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/bar-chart.json
```

## Usage

BarChart.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { BarChart } from '@/components/dissolve/bar-chart';

<BarChart
  data={[{ label: 'Mon', value: 8412 }, { label: 'Tue', value: 10230 }]}
  formatValue={(v) => `${v.toLocaleString()} steps`}
  onSelect={(i) => setDay(i)}
/>

<BarChart stacked maxDots={1000} data={[{ label: 'Jan', values: [42, 18, 30] }]} />
```

BarChart.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { BarChart } from '@/components/dissolve/bar-chart';

<BarChart
  data={[{ label: 'Mon', value: 8412 }, { label: 'Tue', value: 10230 }]}
  formatValue={(v) => `${v.toLocaleString()} steps`}
  onSelect={(i) => setDay(i)}
/>

<BarChart stacked maxDots={1000} data={[{ label: 'Jan', values: [42, 18, 30] }]} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `{ label, value?, values? }[]` | `required` | One bar per item. values are segments, bottom to top. Pass a stable array: new data replays the gather. |
| `height` | `number` | `180` | Plot height. The bubble lane and labels come on top. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `grouped` | Text of the bubble. |
| `formatAxis` | `(value: number) => string` | `compact` | Axis labels, e.g. 1.2k. |
| `onSelect` | `(index: number \| null, datum?) => void` |  | Bar under the finger, then null on release. |
| `stacked` | `boolean` | `false` | Draws values as stacked segments. |
| `colors` | `BarToken[]` | `['primary']` | Segment colors as theme tokens. ['chart-1', 'chart-2', 'chart-3'] (pink, violet, yellow) when stacked. |
| `barRadius` | `number` | `6` | Rounding of the top of each dot column. |
| `maxDots` | `number` | `1400` | Dot budget for the whole chart, the grid gets coarser past it. At most 1600. |
| `gap` | `number` | `6` | Space between bars, shrinks on dense charts. |
| `labelEvery` | `number` |  | One label every N bars. Default: all up to 12 bars. |
| `axis` | `boolean` | `true` | Value axis on the right. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | A tick per bar change while scrubbing. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Root classes (margins, padding...). |
| `bubbleClassName` | `string` |  | Bubble classes (background, radius...). |

# MiniPlayer

**MiniPlayer** is an animated mini player component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Now playing pill that opens into a full player as one object, then folds back.

A now playing bar in liquid glass that opens into the full player as one object, then folds back. Width, height, radius, artwork and the glass surface all follow one value, the artwork arcs into place, and a vertical drag drives it 1:1. In the pill the title sits centered beside the artwork and truncates before the controls. Swipe the closed pill sideways to skip.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add mini-player --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/mini-player.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add mini-player --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/mini-player.json
```

## Usage

MiniPlayer.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { MiniPlayer } from '@/components/dissolve/mini-player';

// Liquid glass surface: npx expo install expo-glass-effect
// Last child of a full screen container: it covers it when open.
<MiniPlayer
  title="Night Swim"
  subtitle="Low Tide"
  artwork={cover}
  progress={0.3}
  duration={214}
  playing={playing}
  onPlayPause={toggle}
  onNext={next}
  onPrev={prev}
/>
```

MiniPlayer.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { MiniPlayer } from '@/components/dissolve/mini-player';

// Last child of a positioned container (relative, full screen): it covers it when open.
<MiniPlayer
  title="Night Swim"
  subtitle="Low Tide"
  artwork="/covers/night-swim.jpg"
  progress={0.3}
  duration={214}
  playing={playing}
  onPlayPause={toggle}
  onNext={next}
  onPrev={prev}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `required` | Track title. Centered beside the artwork and truncated before the controls in the pill, it travels to centered below the artwork. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Artist or album. |
| `artwork` | `ImageSource` | `required` | Cover, grows from 40 pt to the player width. |
| `progress` | `number` | `0` | Track progress, 0 to 1. |
| `duration` | `number` |  | Track length in seconds. Shows the elapsed and remaining times. |
| `playing` | `boolean` | `required` | Play or pause glyph. |
| `onPlayPause` | `() => void` | `required` | Play and pause buttons. |
| `onNext / onPrev` | `() => void` |  | Skip buttons and the sideways swipe on the pill. |
| `expanded` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(expanded: boolean) => void` |  | Called when it opens or folds back. |
| `renderExpanded` | `(api: { close }) => ReactNode` |  | Replaces the bottom row of the open player (lyrics, AirPlay, queue). |
| `bottom` | `number` | `24` | Gap under the closed pill, and bottom padding when open. |
| `topInset` | `number` | `60` | Gap left above the open player. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Rigid when it locks open, light on close, a tick crossing halfway. |
| `glass` | `boolean` | `true` | Liquid glass surface (expo-glass-effect, iOS 26+). Falls back to the surface token with a hairline border. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Player surface classes (background, border) for the fallback surface. |

## Source

- React Native: [registry/mini-player.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/mini-player.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/mini-player.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/mini-player.tsx) and [registry/web/mini-player.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/mini-player.core.ts)

# PullToRefresh

**PullToRefresh** is an animated pull to refresh component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Pull a list down: grains gather into a loader, release and the content rebuilds itself.

Wraps a list. Pull it down past the top and grains drift in from scattered positions to gather into a ring, 1:1 with the pull, with a 0.5 rubber band past the threshold. At the threshold the ring closes with a rigid tick. Release past it and the ring spins while onRefresh runs, the list held under it. When the promise settles, the items already there glide to their new place while the list eases back to the top, all on the calm curve, and the ring grains fly to the new items and build them in grains. Nothing new, or onRefresh threw: the grains fall away as dust. Released early, the grains scatter back out. Wrap each item in PullItem with a stable id: the ids there when the refresh starts are remembered, any other one is new. It works for any layout, rows, a bento grid, wrapped cards of any size. On iOS it rides the native overscroll of the scroll view, so nothing fights the scroll.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add pull-to-refresh --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/pull-to-refresh.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add pull-to-refresh --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/pull-to-refresh.json
```

## Usage

PullToRefresh.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { PullToRefresh, PullItem } from '@/components/dissolve/pull-to-refresh';

<PullToRefresh onRefresh={reload}>
  {items.map((item) => (
    <PullItem key={item.id} id={item.id}>
      <Row tx={item} />
    </PullItem>
  ))}
</PullToRefresh>

// Any layout: a bento grid of cards.
<PullToRefresh onRefresh={reload} contentContainerStyle={grid}>
  {cards.map((card) => (
    <PullItem key={card.id} id={card.id} style={{ width: '47%' }} className="h-36 rounded-3xl bg-dissolve-surface p-4">
      <Card card={card} />
    </PullItem>
  ))}
</PullToRefresh>

// Your own list: spread scroll on it.
<PullToRefresh onRefresh={reload} threshold={96} color="accent">
  {(scroll) => (
    <Animated.FlatList
      {...scroll}
      data={items}
      renderItem={({ item }) => <PullItem id={item.id}><Row tx={item} /></PullItem>}
    />
  )}
</PullToRefresh>
```

PullToRefresh.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { PullToRefresh, PullItem } from '@/components/dissolve/pull-to-refresh';

<PullToRefresh onRefresh={reload}>
  {items.map((item) => (
    <PullItem key={item.id} id={item.id}>
      <Row tx={item} />
    </PullItem>
  ))}
</PullToRefresh>

// Any layout: a bento grid of cards.
<PullToRefresh onRefresh={reload} contentContainerStyle={grid}>
  {cards.map((card) => (
    <PullItem key={card.id} id={card.id} style={{ width: '47%' }} className="h-36 rounded-3xl bg-dissolve-surface p-4">
      <Card card={card} />
    </PullItem>
  ))}
</PullToRefresh>

// Your own list: spread scroll on it.
<PullToRefresh onRefresh={reload} threshold={96} color="accent">
  {(scroll) => (
    <Animated.FlatList
      {...scroll}
      data={items}
      renderItem={({ item }) => <PullItem id={item.id}><Row tx={item} /></PullItem>}
    />
  )}
</PullToRefresh>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| (scroll) => ReactNode` | `required` | List content, wrapped in an Animated.ScrollView. Or a render prop: spread scroll on your own Animated.FlatList or Animated.ScrollView. |
| `onRefresh` | `() => Promise<void>` | `required` | Runs while the ring spins. Update your data before it resolves: the new items are built right after. |
| `threshold` | `number` | `80` | Pull distance that arms the refresh, also the height held while it runs. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Rigid when the ring closes, Success when done, Warning if onRefresh throws. |
| `color` | `PullToken` | `'foreground'` | Grain color as a theme token: 'foreground', 'muted', 'primary', 'accent', 'success', 'chart-1', 'chart-2'. |
| `rebuild` | `boolean` | `true` | Build the new PullItems from the ring grains when the refresh lands. Off, they just show. Needs DissolveProvider. |
| `contentContainerStyle` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` |  | Content container of the built in ScrollView (plain children only). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Root classes (background, radius, margins...). |
| `PullItem` | `{ id, className?, style? }` |  | Wrap each item of the content. id: stable key of the item, any id not there when the refresh started is new. className and style draw the item (captured with it); size and position keys of style (width, flex, margin...) go to its outer box. |

- React: [registry/web/pull-to-refresh.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/pull-to-refresh.tsx) and [registry/web/pull-to-refresh.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/pull-to-refresh.core.ts)

# ReorderList

**ReorderList** is an animated reorder list component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Long press a row to lift it, drag to reorder, the others make room, it settles with a tick.

A list you reorder by drag, like Reminders or Things. Long press a row (250 ms) or grab its handle: it lifts with a medium tick, grows a shadow and leans a little with the sideways speed of the finger, which it follows 1:1. The other rows slide out of the way on the calm curve, a selection tick lands on every new slot, and the list scrolls by itself near its edges. On release the row settles critically damped, then onReorder runs. A faint trail of grains stays at the slot it left, a small puff marks the one it lands in. With onDelete, drag a row far to the side to turn it to dust. Rows can have different heights, everything runs on the UI thread.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add reorder-list --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/reorder-list.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add reorder-list --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/reorder-list.json
```

## Usage

ReorderList.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { ReorderList, ReorderHandle } from '@/components/dissolve/reorder-list';

<ReorderList
  data={tasks}
  keyExtractor={(t) => t.id}
  onReorder={(next) => setTasks(next)}
  onDelete={(t) => remove(t.id)}
  gap={8}
  itemClassName="rounded-[18px] bg-dissolve-surface"
  renderItem={({ item, index }) => (
    <TaskRow task={item} rank={index + 1}>
      <ReorderHandle />
    </TaskRow>
  )}
/>
```

ReorderList.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { ReorderList, ReorderHandle } from '@/components/dissolve/reorder-list';

<ReorderList
  data={tasks}
  keyExtractor={(t) => t.id}
  onReorder={(next) => setTasks(next)}
  onDelete={(t) => remove(t.id)}
  gap={8}
  itemClassName="rounded-[18px] bg-dissolve-surface"
  renderItem={({ item, index }) => (
    <TaskRow task={item} rank={index + 1}>
      <ReorderHandle />
    </TaskRow>
  )}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `T[]` | `required` | The rows, in order. |
| `keyExtractor` | `(item: T, index: number) => string` | `required` | A stable key per row. Rows are positioned by key. |
| `renderItem` | `({ item, index, dragging }) => ReactNode` | `required` | A row. dragging is true while it is lifted (one render on lift, one on drop). |
| `onReorder` | `(data: T[], from: number, to: number) => void` | `required` | Called once the dropped row has settled, with the reordered copy of data. |
| `onDelete` | `(item: T, index: number) => void` |  | Enables the delete: drag a row past 42 percent of the width to the side and release, it turns to dust and the list closes up. |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Exit used by onDelete. |
| `longPressDelay` | `number` | `250` | Hold before a row lifts, ms. Moving earlier scrolls the list instead. |
| `handle` | `boolean` | `false` | Drag only from a `<ReorderHandle>` inside the row, which lifts at once. |
| `gap` | `number` | `0` | Space between rows. Use it instead of vertical margins. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Medium on lift, a selection tick per slot, light on drop. |
| `grains` | `boolean` | `true` | Trail and puff of grains. Off with reduced motion, as is the lean. |
| `header / footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Scroll above and below the rows. |
| `className` | `string` | `'flex-1'` | Root classes. Give the list a height: it scrolls by itself. |
| `contentContainerStyle` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` |  | Scroll content padding. |
| `itemClassName` | `string` | `'bg-dissolve-background'` | Row surface classes (background, radius). The lift shadow follows it. |

# ScratchCard

**ScratchCard** is an animated scratch card component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Glossy foil scratch card that tilts in 3D under the finger, sheds grains, then dissolves past the threshold.

A lottery style card with a metal foil over any content: a reward, a promo code. The foil is one shader, a brushed silver gradient with a fine grain, a faint holographic tint, a bevel lit along the edge and a specular band. The whole card tilts in 3D under the finger, up to 9 degrees with perspective, and the light moves with it, then it springs back flat on release. Scratching erases the foil along a ragged stroke, like a coin or a nail (chipped stamps, a width that follows the speed, rough ends), and sheds it as grains that flick off and fall, with light selection ticks. A coarse grid tracks the scratched share: past the threshold, the rest of the foil dissolves from the last touch, Success haptic, onReveal. Reduced motion keeps the card flat and fades the foil instead.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add scratch-card --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/scratch-card.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add scratch-card --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/scratch-card.json
```

## Usage

ScratchCard.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { ScratchCard } from '@/components/dissolve/scratch-card';

<ScratchCard onReveal={claim}>
  <Text className="text-[40px] font-bold text-dissolve-foreground">$25</Text>
</ScratchCard>

// Gold foil, a bigger brush, reset from a ref.
const card = useRef<ScratchCardHandle>(null);
<ScratchCard ref={card} color="#D9B26F" label="Scratch for your code" brush={44} threshold={0.6}>
  <PromoCode code="SPRING25" />
</ScratchCard>
card.current?.reset();
```

ScratchCard.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { ScratchCard } from '@/components/dissolve/scratch-card';

<ScratchCard onReveal={claim}>
  <span className="text-[40px] font-bold text-dissolve-foreground">$25</span>
</ScratchCard>

// Gold foil, a bigger brush, reset from a ref.
const card = useRef<ScratchCardHandle>(null);
<ScratchCard ref={card} color="#D9B26F" label="Scratch for your code" brush={44} threshold={0.6}>
  <PromoCode code="SPRING25" />
</ScratchCard>
card.current?.reset();
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What the foil hides, centered on the card. |
| `width / height` | `number` | `320 / 200` | Card size in points. |
| `radius` | `number` | `24` | Corner radius. |
| `color` | `string` | `'#C3C8D0'` | Foil base color. A warm tone like #D9B26F gives gold. |
| `label` | `string` | `'Scratch to reveal'` | Text printed on the foil, erased with it. Empty hides it. |
| `brush` | `number` | `38` | Scratch stroke width in points. |
| `threshold` | `number` | `0.55` | Share of the foil to scratch before the rest dissolves. |
| `tilt` | `number` | `9` | Max tilt in degrees under the finger. 0 keeps the card flat. Off under reduced motion. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Selection ticks while scratching, Success on reveal. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No scratching, the card still shows. |
| `onReveal` | `() => void` |  | Called once the foil is gone. |
| `onScratchStart` | `() => void` |  | Called on the first stroke after mount or reset. |
| `className / contentClassName` | `string` |  | Card classes (background, border...) and the classes of the box that centers the children. |
| `ref` | `ScratchCardHandle` |  | reset() puts the foil back, reveal() dissolves it now, progress() gives the scratched share. |

# Skeleton

**Skeleton** is an animated skeleton component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Loading placeholders that break into grains and recompose into the real content, block by block.

Loading placeholders that do not just crossfade. While loading, a calm wave of light rolls across the blocks, top left to bottom right. When loading turns false, every placeholder breaks into grains and those same grains recompose the real content, block by block in reading order (about 70 ms apart, compressed so the whole handoff stays under 900 ms), with one light haptic as the first grains land. The content shows exactly where its grains land. You describe the placeholders and keep your content: wrap each piece in SkeletonBlock with its shape while loading, a line (a rounded bar centered in its line height, lines for a paragraph), a circle (an avatar) or a rect (an image, a card). Children only render once loading is false, so they can read data that is not there yet. Reduced motion: no wave, a short crossfade.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add skeleton --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/skeleton.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add skeleton --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/skeleton.json
```

## Usage

Skeleton.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { Skeleton, SkeletonBlock } from '@/components/dissolve/skeleton';

<Skeleton loading={!user}>
  <View className="flex-row items-center gap-4">
    <SkeletonBlock shape="circle" size={64}>
      <Image source={user?.avatar} style={{ width: 64, height: 64, borderRadius: 32 }} />
    </SkeletonBlock>
    <View className="flex-1 gap-1">
      <SkeletonBlock width={160} height={25}>
        <Text className="text-[20px] font-semibold">{user?.name}</Text>
      </SkeletonBlock>
      <SkeletonBlock width={96}>
        <Text className="text-[15px] text-dissolve-muted">{user?.handle}</Text>
      </SkeletonBlock>
    </View>
  </View>
</Skeleton>

// The dotted form, a cover and a paragraph.
<Skeleton loading={loading} stagger={80} onReveal={() => track('feed_shown')}>
  <Skeleton.Block shape="rect" height={180} radius={20}>
    <Cover post={post} />
  </Skeleton.Block>
  <Skeleton.Block lines={3} height={22} className="mt-3">
    <Text>{post?.body}</Text>
  </Skeleton.Block>
</Skeleton>
```

Skeleton.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { Skeleton, SkeletonBlock } from '@/components/dissolve/skeleton';

<Skeleton loading={!user}>
  <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
    <SkeletonBlock shape="circle" size={64}>
      <img src={user?.avatar} alt="" width={64} height={64} className="rounded-full" />
    </SkeletonBlock>
    <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-1">
      <SkeletonBlock width={160} height={25}>
        <span className="text-[20px] font-semibold">{user?.name}</span>
      </SkeletonBlock>
      <SkeletonBlock width={96}>
        <span className="text-[15px] text-dissolve-muted">{user?.handle}</span>
      </SkeletonBlock>
    </div>
  </div>
</Skeleton>

// The dotted form, a cover and a paragraph.
<Skeleton loading={loading} stagger={80} onReveal={() => track('feed_shown')}>
  <Skeleton.Block shape="rect" height={180} radius={20}>
    <Cover post={post} />
  </Skeleton.Block>
  <Skeleton.Block lines={3} height={22} className="mt-3">
    <p>{post?.body}</p>
  </Skeleton.Block>
</Skeleton>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `required` | True shows the placeholders. False hands every block over to its content in grains. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | `required` | Any layout, with SkeletonBlocks anywhere inside it. |
| `shimmer` | `boolean` | `true` | Wave of light across the blocks while loading. Off under reduced motion. |
| `color` | `'surface' \| 'surface-2' \| 'border'` | `'surface'` | Placeholder fill as a theme token. |
| `stagger` | `number` | `70` | Delay between two blocks in ms, in reading order. Compressed with many blocks so the handoff stays under about 900 ms. |
| `duration` | `number` | `600` | Duration of one block's handoff in ms. |
| `grain` | `number` | `3` | Grain size in points. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | One light impact as the first grains land. |
| `onReveal` | `() => void` |  | Called once every block shows its content. |
| `className / style` | `string / ViewStyle` |  | Root classes and style. |
| `SkeletonBlock` | `{ shape?, width?, height?, size?, radius?, lines?, className?, style? }` |  | Wraps one piece of content. shape: 'line' (default, a bar 0.6 of height, height default 20), 'circle' (size across, default 40) or 'rect' (width by height, default 100% by 120, radius 12). lines stacks bars for a paragraph. className restyles the placeholder, style goes to the outer box. Also available as Skeleton.Block. |

- React Native: [registry/skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/skeleton.tsx)
- React: [registry/web/skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/skeleton.tsx) and [registry/web/skeleton.core.ts](https://github.com/dissolve-ui/dissolve/blob/main/registry/web/skeleton.core.ts)

# SegmentedControl

**SegmentedControl** is an animated segmented control component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. iOS segmented control whose pill breaks into grains, flows to the new segment and reassembles. Drag across to follow the finger.

An iOS style segmented control whose selection pill is made of grains. At rest it is a clean solid capsule with the soft iOS shadow, on a translucent track that sits on any background. Pick another segment and the pill breaks into grains, leading edge first: they flow to the new segment on a slight arc, shrinking mid flight, and reassemble into the pill there, in about 400 ms. The labels cross fade between their selected and unselected styles along the way. Drag the finger across the control and the selection follows it, the grains re-aiming from wherever they are, with a selection tick on every change. On iOS the pill and every grain are Animated views moved by transform and opacity only, so it keeps animating inside a scroll view that is being dragged. Reduced motion: the pill simply slides.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add segmented-control --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/segmented-control.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add segmented-control --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/segmented-control.json
```

## Usage

SegmentedControl.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from '@/components/dissolve/segmented-control';

const [period, setPeriod] = useState('Week');
<SegmentedControl segments={['Day', 'Week', 'Month', 'Year']} value={period} onChange={setPeriod} />

// Smaller, uncontrolled, a fixed width.
<SegmentedControl segments={['Inbox', 'Archive']} defaultValue="Inbox" size="sm" className="w-56 self-center" />

// Items with icons.
<SegmentedControl
  segments={[
    { value: 'list', label: 'List', icon: ({ color, size }) => <ListIcon color={color} size={size} /> },
    { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid', icon: ({ color, size }) => <GridIcon color={color} size={size} /> },
  ]}
  value={layout}
  onChange={setLayout}
/>
```

SegmentedControl.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from '@/components/dissolve/segmented-control';

const [period, setPeriod] = useState('Week');
<SegmentedControl segments={['Day', 'Week', 'Month', 'Year']} value={period} onChange={setPeriod} />

// Smaller, uncontrolled, a fixed width.
<SegmentedControl segments={['Inbox', 'Archive']} defaultValue="Inbox" size="sm" className="w-56 self-center" />

// Items with icons.
<SegmentedControl
  segments={[
    { value: 'list', label: 'List', icon: ({ color, size }) => <ListIcon color={color} size={size} /> },
    { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid', icon: ({ color, size }) => <GridIcon color={color} size={size} /> },
  ]}
  value={layout}
  onChange={setLayout}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` | `(string \| SegmentItem)[]` | `required` | The segments: plain strings, or { value, label?, icon? } items. icon is a node or a function of { color, size, selected }. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Selected value (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `first segment` | Initial value when uncontrolled. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string, index: number) => void` |  | Called on every selection change, also while dragging across the segments. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Height, inset and type size: 30, 36 or 44 pt. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Selection tick on every change. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No selection, the control shows at half opacity. |
| `trackColor` | `string` | `foreground at low alpha` | Track fill. |
| `indicatorColor` | `string` | `background / lifted gray` | Pill and grain color. Default: the background token in light mode, a gray lifted off the track in dark mode. |
| `className / labelClassName` | `string` |  | Track classes (width, margins, self alignment...) and label classes. It stretches to its parent by default. |

# Toggle

**Toggle** is an animated toggle component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. iOS switch whose thumb breaks into grains, flows to the other end of the track and reassembles while the track fills.

An iOS style switch whose thumb is made of grains. At rest it is the familiar white thumb on a capsule track. Flip it and the thumb breaks into grains, leading edge first: they flow to the other end of the track on a slight arc, shrinking mid flight, and reassemble into the thumb there in about 380 ms, while the track fills with the on color behind them. Tap it, or swipe the thumb toward the other side, with a selection tick on every flip. On iOS the thumb, the track layers and every grain are Animated views moved by transform and opacity only, so it keeps animating inside a scroll view that is being dragged. Reduced motion: the thumb simply slides.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add toggle --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/toggle.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add toggle --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/toggle.json
```

## Usage

Toggle.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { Toggle } from '@/components/dissolve/toggle';

const [wifi, setWifi] = useState(true);
<Toggle value={wifi} onValueChange={setWifi} accessibilityLabel="Wi-Fi" />

// Uncontrolled, smaller, another on color.
<Toggle defaultValue size="sm" onColor="#0A84FF" />
```

Toggle.tsx (React):

```tsx

const [wifi, setWifi] = useState(true);
<Toggle value={wifi} onValueChange={setWifi} accessibilityLabel="Wi-Fi" />

// Uncontrolled, smaller, another on color.
<Toggle defaultValue size="sm" onColor="#0A84FF" />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `boolean` |  | On or off (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial state when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new state on every flip. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Track size: 42 x 26, 51 x 31 (the iOS switch) or 60 x 36 pt. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Selection tick on every flip. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No flip, the switch shows at half opacity. |
| `onColor` | `string` | `success token` | Track fill when on. |
| `offColor` | `string` | `foreground at low alpha` | Track fill when off. |
| `thumbColor` | `string` | `white` | Thumb and grain color. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` |  | Read by screen readers. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Outer classes (margins, self alignment...). The size comes from the size prop. |

# ProgressSteps

**ProgressSteps** is an animated progress steps component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Numbered steps on a line, or story style bars: the progress streams on to the next step in grains.

Steps for onboarding, checkout or any multi step form, in two looks. variant="numbers" draws small numbered discs on a hairline: done steps are filled with a check, the current one has a thin ring around it, the next ones are soft and muted. Move forward and the current disc sheds a copy of itself in grains: the cloud flattens onto the line and streams along it, filling the line behind its front, then gathers back into a disc on the new step, in about 450 ms and a little longer when it skips steps. Move back and the disc breaks up and streams home the other way, emptying the line. variant="bars" is story style: one thin segment per step and no numbers. The fill runs on into the next segment, its head gathering out of grains that drift in and settle, and recedes shedding them as dust when you go back. A selection tick on every change. On iOS the discs, fills and every grain are Animated views moved by transform and opacity only, so it keeps animating inside a scroll view that is being dragged. Reduced motion: the fills slide and the discs cross fade.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add progress-steps --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/progress-steps.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add progress-steps --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/progress-steps.json
```

## Usage

ProgressSteps.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { ProgressSteps } from '@/components/dissolve/progress-steps';

const [step, setStep] = useState(0);
<ProgressSteps steps={['Account', 'Profile', 'Payment', 'Done']} current={step} />

// Numbers only, smaller, done steps can be pressed to go back.
<ProgressSteps steps={5} current={step} size="sm" onStepPress={(i) => i < step && setStep(i)} />

// Story bars, no numbers.
<ProgressSteps variant="bars" steps={4} current={story} />
```

ProgressSteps.tsx (React):

```tsx
import { ProgressSteps } from '@/components/dissolve/progress-steps';

const [step, setStep] = useState(0);
<ProgressSteps steps={['Account', 'Profile', 'Payment', 'Done']} current={step} />

// Numbers only, smaller, done steps can be pressed to go back.
<ProgressSteps steps={5} current={step} size="sm" onStepPress={(i) => i < step && setStep(i)} />

// Story bars, no numbers.
<ProgressSteps variant="bars" steps={4} current={story} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'numbers' \| 'bars'` | `'numbers'` | Numbered discs on a line, or story style segments with no numbers. |
| `steps` | `string[] \| number` | `required` | The steps: their labels, or how many there are (no labels then). Two or more. |
| `current` | `number` | `required` | The current step, from 0. steps.length marks them all done. |
| `onStepPress` | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called with the index of a pressed step. Steps are not pressable without it. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Disc, line and type size (18, 22 or 28 pt discs), or bar thickness (3, 4 or 6 pt). |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Selection tick on every change of current. |
| `activeColor` | `string` | `primary token` | Fill of the done and current discs, the line and the grains. |
| `trackColor` | `string` | `foreground at low alpha` | The next steps' discs, the empty line and the empty bars. |
| `className / labelClassName` | `string` |  | Outer classes (width, margins...) and label classes. It stretches to its parent by default. |

# ElasticSlider

**ElasticSlider** is an animated elastic slider component for React Native and React, from the dissolve library. Thick rounded slider whose texts invert over the fill; pulled past an end, the track stretches like a rubber band and snaps back.

A thick, rounded slider in the spirit of the iOS Control Center. The fill grows from the left, a label sits on the left and the value on the right, both inverting their color exactly where the fill passes under them. Drag anywhere to move it by the finger's distance, or tap to jump. Pull past either end and the whole track stretches like a rubber band toward the finger, thinning a little, then snaps back with a bounce on release. The value rolls digit by digit. A tick when it reaches the minimum or the maximum, and on every step when there are 20 steps or fewer. On iOS everything moves by transform only, so it keeps animating inside a scroll view that is being dragged.

## Install

### React Native

Install the engine once per app and wrap the root layout in `<DissolveProvider>` (see [Installation](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/docs/installation/)), then copy the component into `components/dissolve`:

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add elastic-slider --native
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/native/elastic-slider.json
```

### React

Needs React 19 and `react-dom`, nothing else: no engine, no provider, no Tailwind. Works in the Next.js App Router.

```sh
npx dissolve-ui add elastic-slider --web
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://dissolve.rselmi.com/r/elastic-slider.json
```

## Usage

ElasticSlider.tsx (React Native):

```tsx
import { ElasticSlider } from '@/components/dissolve/elastic-slider';

const [volume, setVolume] = useState(40);
<ElasticSlider label="Volume" value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} formatValue={(v) => `${v}%`} />

// An icon before the label, drawn in the color it gets (it inverts over the fill).
<ElasticSlider label="Brightness" icon={({ color, size }) => <SunIcon color={color} size={size} />} defaultValue={70} />

// A small stepped one, no value shown.
<ElasticSlider min={0} max={10} step={1} defaultValue={4} size="sm" showValue={false} />
```

ElasticSlider.tsx (React):

```tsx

<ElasticSlider label="Volume" value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} formatValue={(v) => `${v}%`} />

// An icon before the label, drawn in the color it gets (it inverts over the fill).
<ElasticSlider label="Brightness" icon={({ color, size }) => <SunIcon color={color} size={size} />} defaultValue={70} />

// A small stepped one, no value shown.
<ElasticSlider min={0} max={10} step={1} defaultValue={4} size="sm" showValue={false} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` |  | Current value (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | `min` | Initial value when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called with the stepped value while sliding, every time it changes. |
| `onSlidingComplete` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called with the final value when the finger lifts. |
| `min / max / step` | `number` | `0 / 100 / 1` | Range and step. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Text on the left of the track. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode \| ({ color, size }) => ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label. As a function it gets the color it should be drawn in, which inverts over the fill. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the value on the right of the track. |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `the number` | Turns the value into the shown text. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Track height and type size: 32, 44 or 56 pt. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Ticks at the ends, and on every step when there are 20 steps or fewer. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No sliding, the track shows at half opacity. |
| `fillColor` | `string` | `foreground token` | Fill color. |
| `trackColor` | `string` | `foreground at low alpha` | Empty track color. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Outer classes (width, margins...). It stretches to its parent by default. |

# Dust

**Dust** is one of the 16 effects of dissolve, an animation library for React Native. Any view snapshots into grains that drift away on the wind, left edge first. It runs with `useDissolve` from `dissolve-ui`.

## Usage

Dust (React Native):

```tsx
import { useDissolve } from 'dissolve-ui';

const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();

<View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>
  <Card />
</View>

await dissolve({
  preset: 'dust',
  grain: 3,
  duration: 1500,
});
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Set it to `'dust'`. |
| `grain` | `number` | `3` | Grain size in points. Raised automatically past about 6000 grains per burst. |
| `duration` | `number` | `1500` | Full effect length in ms. |
| `origin` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'center' \| { x, y }` | `none` | Where the wind starts. Without it grains leave left to right with a slight lift. |
| `direction` | `'out' \| 'in'` | `'out'` | `'in'` plays it backwards as an entrance. Use `DissolveIn` or `useAppear` for that. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Soft impact, then a few ticks while the wave sweeps the view. |
| `field` | `'cascade'` | `none` | Replaces the native delay with a diagonal wave, for lists and full screens. |
| `rows` | `number[]` | `none` | Row boundaries in local Y used by `field: 'cascade'`: rows leave one after the other. |

## Best practices

- Use it for light, reversible removals: clearing a notification, archiving a row, dismissing a toast.
- Keep grain at 2 to 4 pt on cards and rows. Below 2 pt a large view hits the 6000 grain cap and the grain is raised for you.
- Hide the original with `opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1` and remove it from state after the `await`.
- Do not chain several dust exits on screen at once, a cascade on one snapshot reads better and costs one burst.
- Reduced motion is handled by the provider: the effect is skipped and the promise resolves at once, so keep your state update after the `await`.

## Install

Install the package and its peers, then wrap the app once in `<DissolveProvider>`, above the navigator.

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

app/_layout.tsx:

```tsx
import { Stack } from 'expo-router';
import { GestureHandlerRootView } from 'react-native-gesture-handler';
import { DissolveProvider } from 'dissolve-ui';

export default function Layout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <DissolveProvider>
        <Stack />
      </DissolveProvider>
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

Next: [Sand](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/effects/sand/) · [All effects](https://dissolve.rselmi.com/effects/)

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/effects/dust/

Source: https://dissolve.rselmi.com/effects/sand/

# Sand

**Sand** is one of the 16 effects of dissolve, an animation library for React Native. Grains pour straight down with gravity and slide out of frame. It runs with `useDissolve` from `dissolve-ui`.

## Usage

Sand (React Native):

```tsx
import { useDissolve } from 'dissolve-ui';

const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();

<View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>
  <Card />
</View>

await dissolve({
  preset: 'sand',
  grain: 2.5,
  duration: 1500,
});
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Set it to `'sand'`. |
| `grain` | `number` | `2.5` | Grain size in points. Raised automatically past about 6000 grains per burst. |
| `duration` | `number` | `1500` | Full effect length in ms. |
| `origin` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'center' \| { x, y }` | `none` | Where the pour starts. Without it columns fall left to right. |
| `direction` | `'out' \| 'in'` | `'out'` | `'in'` plays it backwards as an entrance. Use `DissolveIn` or `useAppear` for that. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Soft impact, then a few ticks while the wave sweeps the view. |
| `field` | `'cascade'` | `none` | Replaces the native delay with a diagonal wave, for lists and full screens. |
| `rows` | `number[]` | `none` | Row boundaries in local Y used by `field: 'cascade'`: rows leave one after the other. |

## Best practices

- Fits deletes with weight: photos, files, anything that should fall rather than blow away.
- Keep 2 to 3 pt grain on photos so the image still reads as it pours.
- Avoid it near the bottom edge of the screen, the pour needs room below the view.
- Use 1200 to 1800 ms. Shorter feels like a glitch, longer blocks the next action.
- Reduced motion is handled by the provider: the effect is skipped and the promise resolves at once, so keep your state update after the `await`.

## Install

Install the package and its peers, then wrap the app once in `<DissolveProvider>`, above the navigator.

```sh

```

```tsx

import { DissolveProvider } from 'dissolve-ui';

export default function Layout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <DissolveProvider>
        <Stack />
      </DissolveProvider>
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

# Ember

**Ember** is one of the 16 effects of dissolve, an animation library for React Native. Burns from the edge and rises as sparks tinted by the view itself. It runs with `useDissolve` from `dissolve-ui`.

## Usage

Ember (React Native):

```tsx
import { useDissolve } from 'dissolve-ui';

const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();

<View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>
  <Card />
</View>

await dissolve({
  preset: 'ember',
  grain: 3,
  duration: 1500,
});
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Set it to `'ember'`. |
| `grain` | `number` | `3` | Grain size in points. Raised automatically past about 6000 grains per burst. |
| `duration` | `number` | `1500` | Full effect length in ms. |
| `origin` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'center' \| { x, y }` | `none` | Where the burn starts. Without it it burns from the left, bottom first. |
| `direction` | `'out' \| 'in'` | `'out'` | `'in'` plays it backwards as an entrance. Use `DissolveIn` or `useAppear` for that. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Soft impact, then a few ticks while the wave sweeps the view. |
| `field` | `'cascade'` | `none` | Replaces the native delay with a diagonal wave, for lists and full screens. |
| `rows` | `number[]` | `none` | Row boundaries in local Y used by `field: 'cascade'`: rows leave one after the other. |

## Best practices

- Use it for permanent removals with a bit of drama: burn after reading, discard a draft, revoke a key.
- Sparks are tinted by the dominant color of the view, colorful views glow best.
- Do not use it for routine actions like marking as read, it reads as destructive.
- Keep haptics on: the sweep ticks match the burn front.
- Reduced motion is handled by the provider: the effect is skipped and the promise resolves at once, so keep your state update after the `await`.

## Install

Install the package and its peers, then wrap the app once in `<DissolveProvider>`, above the navigator.

# Pixel

**Pixel** is one of the 16 effects of dissolve, an animation library for React Native. A blocky, stepped collapse for retro and game UIs. It runs with `useDissolve` from `dissolve-ui`.

## Usage

Pixel (React Native):

```tsx
import { useDissolve } from 'dissolve-ui';

const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();

<View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>
  <Card />
</View>

await dissolve({
  preset: 'pixel',
  grain: 7,
  duration: 1500,
});
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Set it to `'pixel'`. |
| `grain` | `number` | `7` | Grain size in points. Raised automatically past about 6000 grains per burst. |
| `duration` | `number` | `1500` | Full effect length in ms. |
| `origin` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'center' \| { x, y }` | `none` | Where the collapse starts. Without it blocks fall in random order. |
| `direction` | `'out' \| 'in'` | `'out'` | `'in'` plays it backwards as an entrance. Use `DissolveIn` or `useAppear` for that. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Soft impact, then a few ticks while the wave sweeps the view. |
| `field` | `'cascade'` | `none` | Replaces the native delay with a diagonal wave, for lists and full screens. |
| `rows` | `number[]` | `none` | Row boundaries in local Y used by `field: 'cascade'`: rows leave one after the other. |

## Best practices

- Made for games, retro skins and playful UIs: level cleared, enemy down, coin collected.
- Use a larger grain (6 to 10 pt). The stepped motion needs visible blocks.
- Avoid it on photos in a calm interface, it reads as a rendering bug there.
- Short durations (800 to 1200 ms) suit the stepped timing.
- Reduced motion is handled by the provider: the effect is skipped and the promise resolves at once, so keep your state update after the `await`.

## Install

Install the package and its peers, then wrap the app once in `<DissolveProvider>`, above the navigator.

```sh
npx expo install dissolve-ui @shopify/react-native-skia react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics
```

app/_layout.tsx:

```tsx
import { Stack } from 'expo-router';
import { GestureHandlerRootView } from 'react-native-gesture-handler';
import { DissolveProvider } from 'dissolve-ui';

export default function Layout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <DissolveProvider>
        <Stack />
      </DissolveProvider>
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

# Vortex

**Vortex** is one of the 16 effects of dissolve, an animation library for React Native. Grains spiral into the center and vanish. It runs with `useDissolve` from `dissolve-ui`.

## Usage

Vortex (React Native):

```tsx
import { useDissolve } from 'dissolve-ui';

const { ref, dissolving, dissolve } = useDissolve();

<View ref={ref} collapsable={false} style={{ opacity: dissolving ? 0 : 1 }}>
  <Card />
</View>

await dissolve({
  preset: 'vortex',
  grain: 3,
  duration: 1500,
});
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `VariantName` | `'dust'` | Set it to `'vortex'`. |
| `grain` | `number` | `3` | Grain size in points. Raised automatically past about 6000 grains per burst. |
| `duration` | `number` | `1500` | Full effect length in ms. |
| `origin` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'center' \| { x, y }` | `none` | Where the spiral starts. Without it the edges go first and the center last. |
| `direction` | `'out' \| 'in'` | `'out'` | `'in'` plays it backwards as an entrance. Use `DissolveIn` or `useAppear` for that. |
| `haptics` | `boolean` | `true` | Soft impact, then a few ticks while the wave sweeps the view. |
| `field` | `'cascade'` | `none` | Replaces the native delay with a diagonal wave, for lists and full screens. |
| `rows` | `number[]` | `none` | Row boundaries in local Y used by `field: 'cascade'`: rows leave one after the other. |

## Best practices

- Use it for clear all and close actions: the view collapses toward a single point.
- Set an origin to collapse toward a button or a badge rather than the center.
- Avoid very wide views, the spiral flattens on long thin shapes.
- 3 pt grain and 1500 ms is the sweet spot on cards.
- Reduced motion is handled by the provider: the effect is skipped and the promise resolves at once, so keep your state update after the `await`.

## Install


```tsx
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <DissolveProvider>
```
